title: [Immediate autologous breast reconstruction by profund artery perforator flap at the expense of the profund femoral artery: Technique and results (IBR by PAP)].
abstract: The profunda artery perforator (PAP) free flap, introduced for breast reconstruction by Allen in 2012, has become an increasingly important autologous option, particularly in immediate breast reconstruction (IBR). Anatomy and technique The PAP flap relies on perforators from the profunda femoris artery, consistently present in 98.8% of cases, with a mean diameter of 1.9mm and a pedicle length of 10 to 12cm. The fasciocutaneous paddle is harvested from the posteromedial thigh, below the infragluteal fold, with the patient in the dorsal lithotomy position, an approach that enables a two-team setup with simultaneous flap harvest and mastectomy with preparation of the internal mammary vessels. Preoperative planning relies on CT angiography and Doppler ultrasound to select the optimal perforator based on caliber, location, and course. Microsurgical anastomoses are performed to the internal mammary vessels. Mean flap volume is approximately 325cm 3 , and secondary fat grafting is performed in nearly all cases to achieve the desired final volume. Clinical cases Two patients illustrate the technical variants: the first (42 years old, recurrence following lumpectomy and radiotherapy) underwent flat flap inset to replace the resected skin; the second (46 years old, similar oncological context) had a cone-shaped flap modeled to allow immediate nipple-areola complex (NAC) reconstruction, with stable outcomes at 3years following fat grafting and areola dermopigmentation. Outcomes and indications Recent meta-analyses report total failure rates of 2% and fat necrosis rates of 6.1%. Donor-site morbidity remains moderate, with wound dehiscence occurring in 10 to 21% of cases. With over 14 years of follow-up, the PAP flap represents the best autologous alternative to the DIEP flap in IBR, combining anatomical reliability, absence of functional muscle morbidity, and a well-concealed donor-site scar.

title: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation.
abstract: Introduction and objectives Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value. Patients and methods All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT. Results The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001). Conclusions Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

title: AI model integrating dosimetric and radiomic features for predicting cognitive impairment after brain radiotherapy.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is one of the most debilitating late effects of brain radiotherapy, affecting memory, attention, and executive function in a substantial proportion of survivors. Accurate prospective identification of patients at high risk would enable adaptive dose constraints, prophylactic neuroprotective interventions, and personalised cognitive rehabilitation planning.To develop and validate a multimodal artificial intelligence model that integrates dosimetric parameters, MRI-derived radiomic features, and clinical variables for predicting radiation-induced cognitive impairment at six months after completion of brain radiotherapy.A retrospective cohort of 412 patients who received brain radiotherapy between 2016 and 2023 was assembled from two tertiary neuro-oncology centres. Cognitive impairment was defined as a decline of at least 1.5 standard deviations from baseline on at least two domains of a standardised neuropsychological battery at six months. Dosimetric features were extracted from treatment planning systems for seven organs at risk. Radiomic features (n = 1316) were extracted from pre-treatment T1-weighted and T2-FLAIR MRI using PyRadiomics. Feature selection combined LASSO regression with recursive feature elimination. A gradient-boosted ensemble model with attention-based feature fusion was trained on 289 patients and independently validated on 123 patients. The proposed AI Fusion model achieved an AUC of 0.871 (95% CI 0.821-0.921) on the independent validation set, significantly outperforming dosimetric-only (AUC 0.714), radiomic-only (AUC 0.748), and clinical-only (AUC 0.682) models. Sensitivity was 81.4% and specificity was 79.6% at the optimal threshold. SHAP analysis identified mean hippocampal dose (D_mean), wavelet-LLH first-order energy from hippocampal region, GLCM entropy, and V30Gy as the four most predictive features. Decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit superiority of the fusion model across threshold probabilities from 15% to 75%. Integrating dosimetric and radiomic features into a gradient-boosted AI model substantially improves prediction of cognitive impairment after brain radiotherapy. The model provides a clinically actionable risk stratification tool that could guide individualised treatment planning and post-treatment surveillance.

title: Chest computed tomography for oncological follow-Up: Clinical relevance and importance of dosimetric evaluation.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is widely used in oncology for diagnosis, treatment planning, staging, follow-up, and assessment of disease extent. Diagnostic Reference Levels (DRLs) recommend dosimetric metrics based on volume CT dose index (CTDI vol ), dose-length product (DLP), while effective dose (E) was estimated as a complementary indicator for radiation dose comparison and population-based risk assessment. This retrospective study evaluated the importance of chest CT in oncological indications at a public hospital and assessed dosimetrics for radiation protection monitoring. Chest CT examinations performed in elective outpatients during 2025 were analyzed. In the studied sample (n = 1177), almost 64% of patients had oncological clinical indications, with a mean age of 63.69 ± 13.80 years; around 45% were female and 55% male. Dosimetric parameters were obtained from two 64-slice scanners: PHILIPS INCISIVE (CTA) and CANON AQUILION (CTB). Median DLP and CTDI vol values, respectively, were 190.02 mGy cm and 5.24 mGy (CT A), and 146.28 mGy cm and 6.48 mGy (CTB). Effective dose values were 2.67 ± 0.84 mSv (CTA) and 2.36 ± 1.23 mSv (CTB). For oncological chest CT examinations (n=172), CT A presented P25/P50/P75 values of 4.17/5.24/6.21 mGy for CTDI vol and 150.61/190.02/222.70 mGy cm for DLP, whereas CT B presented corresponding values of 3.43/6.48/8.74 mGy for CTDI vol and 91.18/138.93/199.94 mGy cm for DLP. All values remained below International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) reference levels. CTB showed higher dose indices, likely related to a higher tube current-time product. These findings reinforce the importance of continuous dosimetric monitoring to optimize CT protocols and ensure radiation protection in oncological patients. Chest CT remains essential for metastatic evaluation and oncological patient management.

title: Integrating radiomics and dosiomics to predict tumor regression for early adaptive radiotherapy in NSCLC patients.
abstract: Background Although adaptive radiotherapy (ART) has many advantages, its high resource demands limit routine clinical application. Developing prediction models for tumor regression based on radiomics and dosiomics may help identify NSCLC patients who can benefit METHODS: This retrospective study included 116 NSCLC patients. Tumor regression was assessed by the change in gross tumor volume (GTV) after 18-20 fractions. Radiomics and dosiomics features were extracted and fused. Feature selection was performed using random forest, principal component analysis, and XGBoost. SVM models were then constructed based on radiomics, dosiomics, and fused features. Features from the optimal single-omics models were further integrated to develop a combined model. Performance was evaluated via ROC analysis, calibration, and decision curve analysis. For tumor regression sensitive patients, CBCT images were processed to generate synthetic CT (sCT). The 10th-fraction sCT was subsequently used to examine lung dose changes and their association with tumor volume reduction. Results No significant differences were observed in clinical characteristics between the two groups of tumor regression. On the validation set, the combined model achieved the best predictive performance with an AUC of 0.811, outperforming the radiomics, dosiomics, and fused models (AUCs: 0.750, 0.778, 0.756, respectively). The fused model did not show advantages over the single-omics model. At the 10 fraction, lung dose parameters had increased and exhibited a linear correlation with tumor volume reduction, suggesting that early dose variation may serve as potential indicators for ART. Conclusions This study aims to integrate radiomics and dosiomics to construct a predictive model for tumor regression during radiotherapy for NSCLC, with the combined model achieving the best predictive performance. Preliminary dose verification based on CBCT demonstrated the feasibility of early ART for tumor regression sensitive patients.

title: Perceptually optimized NPS-based deep learning framework for PET image denoising.
abstract: Purpose To develop and evaluate a scanner-specific noise power spectrum (NPS)-based framework for deep learning PET image denoising under reduced-count conditions. Methods Retrospective whole-body 18 F-FDG PET/CT datasets from 250 subjects and three scanners were used to train a perceptually optimized 2.5D U-Net. Data were partitioned at the patient level into scanner-specific training, validation, and independent testing subsets. Training strategies included NPS-simulated data (DL-NPS), list-mode reconstructions (DL-LM), and their combination (DL-all). Image quality was evaluated using SSIM, PSNR, RMSE, liver coefficient of variation (CV), lesion contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and SUV agreement. CNR-based lesion visibility was assessed using the Rose Criterion, while three nuclear medicine physicians independently performed blinded image-quality assessments. Results DL-NPS achieved competitive performance relative to LM-trained models across scanner configurations. Denoising improved lesion CNR by 15-38% at 25% and 50% counts, increasing the proportion of lesions meeting the Rose visibility threshold by up to 13.5% after denoising. Liver CV decreased toward standard-count reference levels. Bland-Altman analysis showed limited SUV bias (absolute mean bias ≤0.17, 95% LoA within ±1.1). Reader assessments generally favored DL-denoised images, with significant paired improvements for Biograph Horizon but not Discovery 710 after multiplicity correction. Conclusion Scanner-specific NPS simulation provides a feasible strategy for generating PET denoising training data when LM acquisitions are limited. Larger independent and external studies are required to establish generalizability and clinical applicability.

title: CGHA-Net: Context-guided hybrid attention for hierarchical representation learning in medical image segmentation.
abstract: Medical image segmentation aims to precisely identify and separate anatomical components and lesion regions in medical scans, and it constitutes a core technique for clinical diagnosis, disease evaluation, and organ morphological analysis. However, accurate segmentation of complex anatomical regions remains a significant challenge because of considerable differences in object scale, indistinct boundaries, and insufficient tissue contrast in medical images. These issues often limit the ability of existing methods to effectively exploit global semantic representations while simultaneously retaining detailed local information. Reliable segmentation of organs and lesions remains challenging in practical medical images because low contrast, irregular morphology, and blurred boundaries can obscure target structures and hinder accurate delineation. To address these challenges, we propose a new medical image segmentation framework, termed CGHA-Net. First, a context-guided semantic enhancement module is incorporated into the skip connections, in which deep global semantic information is progressively used to enhance shallow feature representations, thereby improving semantic discriminability while preserving local details. Second, a multidimensional semantic fusion module is introduced in the decoder to enhance contextual feature representations by jointly integrating spatial, channel, and orientation-aware information, thereby enhancing boundary detail reconstruction. Finally, a largest connected component loss is proposed to encourage the continuity and integrity of the segmented regions. Across several public benchmarks for medical image segmentation, overall, CGHA-Net achieves competitive results among leading approaches, suggesting satisfactory effectiveness and generalization capability.

title: Validation of rheumatoid arthritis low inflammatory activity: a novel clinical target quantifying inflammatory disease activity.
abstract: Objectives This study aims to define and validate a state of rheumatoid arthritis low inflammatory activity (RALI) based on previously validated modified disease activity scores, a tool aimed at improving precision of management. Methods We used data from 3 clinical trials (N = 960) and a large real-world study (Veterans Affairs Rheumatoid Arthritis [VARA] Registry; N = 3423). We determined the optimal discriminatory cutoff using receiver-operating-characteristic analyses for each modified score compared with traditional remission at month 6 in a large clinical trial. We then validated each threshold by evaluating clinical characteristics and prognosis (radiographic progression, cardiovascular disease, and death) among those defined as RALI, comparing its performance to traditional clinical remission using descriptive statistics and Cox regression. Results Thresholds for RALI for the Modified Disease Activity Score in 28 Joints (M-DAS28), the Modified Simplified Disease Activity Index, and the Modified Clinical Disease Activity Index were determined to be <1.4, ≤3, and ≤2, respectively. In 3 datasets, a greater number were in RALI compared with the number in remission by traditional scores. RALI was similarly predictive of radiographic progression compared with remission defined by traditional scores. In VARA, M-DAS28 RALI was more common than DAS28 remission (44.0% vs 32.1%). Those in RALI but with high traditional scores had higher rates of comorbidity (eg, anxiety and depression) and lower rates of seropositivity and erosive disease. RALI was a stronger predictor of cardiovascular disease and death than traditional scores. Conclusions More patients achieved RALI than traditional remission with similar or lower rates of radiographic progression as well as low rates of high-risk characteristics and adverse long-term outcomes. These results support RALI as a point-of-care clinical target to inform management.

title: Smaller Lateral Gap Than the Medial Gap in Deep-Flexion was Associated with Lower Patient Satisfaction in Robotic-Assisted Restricted Kinematically Aligned Cruciate-Retaining Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background Medio-lateral soft-tissue balance influences clinical outcomes after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). The purpose of this study was to investigate the intraoperative medial-lateral gap difference pattern in restricted kinematically aligned (rKA) TKA and its associations with radiographic parameters and clinical outcomes. Methods A total of 110 knees were retrospectively analyzed. Robotic-assisted rKA TKA using a cruciate-retaining implant was performed to restore the native joint surface. Preoperative and postoperative radiographic parameters were measured. Intraoperative component gaps were assessed during the implant trial stage. Medial-lateral gap balance was defined as the lateral gap minus the medial gap, with positive values indicating a larger lateral gap than the medial gap. Knees were classified into three groups; group 1 (n = 83; medial gap less than lateral gap consistently), group 2 (n = 11; medial gap greater than lateral gap from extension to mid-flexion), and group 3 (n = 16; medial gap greater than lateral gap from mid-range to deep flexion). Clinical outcomes were evaluated at one year postoperatively using the Knee Society Score (KSS) satisfaction, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index (WOMAC), and Forgotten Joint Score-12. Results Compared with group 3, group 1 showed a significantly higher satisfaction score (30.9 versus 23.5, P < 0.001) and a significantly lower WOMAC pain score (3.4 versus 5.8, P = 0.032). Multiple regression analyses showed that significant risk factors for smaller medial-lateral gap balance were a smaller preoperative angle between the surgical epicondylar axis and the posterior condylar axis (SEA-PCA) (P = 0.003) and the change in SEA-PCA (P < 0.001). Conclusion A smaller lateral gap than the medial gap from mid-range to deep flexion was associated with lower patient satisfaction in robotic-assisted rKA TKA. Femoral component rotation based on gap simulation may help achieve the target medial-lateral gap pattern during flexion. Level of evidence III.

title: Association of Preoperative Hamstring-Popliteal Angle with Postoperative Knee Extension After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Backgroud Optimal knee extension after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is essential for functional recovery. Although intra-articular factors, including preoperative and intraoperative extension status, influence outcomes, the role of extra-articular posterior soft-tissue tension remains unclear. This study investigated associations of preoperative knee extension angle and hamstring-popliteal angle (HPA) with postoperative knee extension and temporal changes after TKA. Methods This retrospective study included 127 patients who had varus knee osteoarthritis who underwent posterior-stabilized TKA. Preoperative posterior soft-tissue tension was assessed by the HPA under anesthesia. The knee extension angle was measured preoperatively, immediately postoperatively, at one month, and at one year using lateral radiographs. Repeated-measures analysis of variance assessed temporal changes, and linear regression was used to evaluate associations. Results The knee extension angle improved significantly over time after TKA (P < 0.001), with substantial inter-individual variability. Preoperative HPA correlated with the preoperative knee extension angle (r = -0.589, P < 0.001), 1-year knee extension (r = -0.508, P < 0.001), and changes in knee extension (r = -0.465, P < 0.001), but not with the immediate postoperative knee extension angle. Multiple regression analysis identified preoperative HPA (β = -0.332, P < 0.001), preoperative knee extension angle (β = 0.292, P = 0.001), and immediate postoperative knee extension angle (β = 0.288, P < 0.001) as factors independently associated with 1-year knee extension (R 2 = 0.430). Changes in knee extension were independently associated with preoperative HPA (β = -0.341, P < 0.001) and preoperative knee extension angle (β = 0.269, P = 0.004) (R 2 = 0.283). Conclusions Preoperative HPA was independently associated with 1-year knee extension and longitudinal changes after TKA. These findings suggest that HPA may provide additional information regarding postoperative extension and its changes over time.

title: Structural-preserving diffusion generation for zero-shot CECT-to-NCCT synthesis.
abstract: Contrast-enhanced and non-contrast computed tomography (CECT/NCCT) are widely used in various clinical scenarios. CECT-to-NCCT synthesis enables NCCT images to be directly generated from CECT images. This streamlines clinical workflows, reduces radiation exposure risk, and prevents co-registration errors. However, to learn the mapping relationship between CECT and NCCT images, existing CECT-to-NCCT synthesis methods typically require supervised settings, which are reliant on substantial paired data. In this paper, we propose a structural preservation diffusion generation (SPDG) method for zero-shot CECT-to-NCCT synthesis. SPDG does not rely on paired data and can be implemented on a pretrained vanilla diffusion model, utilizing an inference-only process to generate NCCT images. Specifically, our SPDG is a guided diffusion generation method that uses the generative prior of the diffusion model and exploits structure-dependent guidance functions to achieve CECT-to-NCCT synthesis. Using guide images from CECT, we design consistency guidance and smoothness constraints as guidance functions for NCCT image generation. Based on the distribution characteristics of the enhanced regions in CECT images, we split the image into a potential enhancement region and an intensity stable region, and designed specific consistency guiding functions for each. The SPDG method is evaluated on abdomen and head and neck datasets, and the results demonstrate that state-of-the-art performance is achieved in unsupervised CECT-to-NCCT synthesis.

title: Rheumatic disease-associated esophageal motility disorders: mechanisms, diagnosis, and therapeutic advances.
abstract: Rheumatic diseases are systemic autoimmune disorders with heterogeneous esophageal manifestations. In this review, "esophageal involvement" refers to symptoms, mucosal disease, and reflux, whereas "esophageal motility disorders (EMDs)" denotes objective manometric abnormalities. Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the greatest burden; idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), Sjögren disease (SjD), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) show distinct and variably documented phenotypes. Current evidence supports a multicomponent pathogenesis involving immune-mediated muscle injury, autonomic and enteric neural dysfunction, smooth-muscle atrophy, microvascular injury, and variable rather than universal fibrosis. High-resolution manometry interpreted with Chicago Classification version 4.0 remains central to diagnosis, complemented by endoscopy, ambulatory pH-impedance monitoring, barium studies, and selected use of functional luminal imaging probe panometry. Management is symptom- and mechanism-directed: proton pump inhibitors are used for documented or symptomatic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), prokinetic therapy may be considered according to the affected gastrointestinal segment and residual motor function, and endoscopic, surgical, and nutritional interventions are individualized. Evidence quality is generally limited by small, selected cohorts and heterogeneous definitions. This review summarizes current knowledge on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, clinical manifestations, and management of esophageal motility disorders associated with rheumatic diseases.

title: Clinical characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin in patients with lower extremity artery disease.
abstract: Objective Elevated circulating adiponectin has been associated with poor prognosis in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD). However, the clinical characteristics underlying elevated adiponectin in patients with LEAD remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify the clinical and computed tomography (CT)-derived body composition characteristics associated with elevated serum adiponectin and to evaluate the association between serum adiponectin and 2-year overall survival in patients with LEAD. Methods This prospective observational study included 80 patients with LEAD who underwent lower extremity revascularization between May 2021 and December 2023. Serum adiponectin levels were measured at the time of revascularization. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, and CT-derived body composition parameters were compared between patients with high and low serum adiponectin levels, classified according to the median value. 2-year overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. The association between serum adiponectin and 2-year mortality was also evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression adjusted for age. Factors associated with serum adiponectin were assessed using univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses. Results Among the 80 patients, 40 were classified into the high adiponectin group and 40 into the low adiponectin group. Patients with high adiponectin were significantly older and had lower body mass index (BMI), visceral fat area (VFA), subcutaneous fat area (SFA), and triglyceride levels than those with low adiponectin. 2-year overall survival was significantly lower in the high adiponectin group than in the low adiponectin group (78.6% vs 94.8%, p = .0330). After adjustment for age, high serum adiponectin remained significantly associated with 2-year mortality (HR = 2.22, 95% CI, 1.08 to 5.83, p = .0278). In multivariable linear regression analysis, VFA remained independently and inversely associated with serum adiponectin after adjustment for age, BMI, skeletal muscle area, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (β = -0.0126 per 10 cm 2 increase, 95% CI, -0.0221 to -0.0032, p = .0096). Conclusion Elevated serum adiponectin was associated with poor 2-year survival in patients with LEAD. Reduced CT-derived VFA was independently associated with elevated serum adiponectin even after adjustment for BMI and other clinical factors. These findings suggest that elevated adiponectin may characterize a LEAD phenotype with reduced visceral adiposity and adverse prognosis.

After adjustment for age, high serum adiponectin remained significantly associated with 2-year mortality (HR = 2.22, 95% CI, 1.08 to 5.83, p = .0278). In multivariable linear regression analysis, VFA remained independently and inversely associated with serum adiponectin after adjustment for age, BMI, skeletal muscle area, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and chronic limb-threatening ischemia (β = -0.0126 per 10 cm2 increase, 95% CI, -0.0221 to -0.0032, p = .0096).

Conclusion

Elevated serum adiponectin was associated with poor 2-year survival in patients with LEAD. Reduced CT-derived VFA was independently associated with elevated serum adiponectin even after adjustment for BMI and other clinical factors. These findings suggest that elevated adiponectin may characterize a LEAD phenotype with reduced visceral adiposity and adverse prognosis.

title: Posterior Transverse Plication of Tortuous Internal Carotid Arteries During Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract: Objectives Excessive tortuosity of the internal carotid artery (ICA) can create a risk of kinking after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) with patch angioplasty. Posterior transverse plication (PTP) shortens and straightens the ICA without arterial transection or resection. This study reviewed our outcomes with PTP followed by patch angioplasty during CEA. Methods A retrospective cohort study identified patients who underwent CEA between 2006 and 2023. Patients treated with PTP and patch angioplasty (PTP+P) were compared with a contemporaneous cohort undergoing CEA with Dacron patch closure alone (DP) for the same atherosclerotic carotid disease. Early and long-term outcomes included neurologic events, restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, and survival. Results Of 168 carotid interventions, 116 met inclusion criteria: 16 PTP+P and 100 DP. Patients in the PTP+P cohort were older and had higher rates of chronic renal insufficiency and coronary artery disease. There was no 30-day mortality or postoperative TIA/stroke in either cohort. During follow-up, no ipsilateral ischemic neurologic event occurred, and there was no significant difference in restenosis, pseudoaneurysm formation, reintervention, or overall survival. In adjusted analysis, increasing age was associated with worse survival, while PTP was not. Conclusions In this small series, adding PTP during CEA before patch angioplasty appeared safe for correcting ICA tortuosity. The complication profile was similar to that of patients with straighter ICAs who underwent DP closure alone. A wide patch and intraoperative duplex ultrasound are advisable to prevent and detect technical narrowing at the plication site. Meshwords Carotid endarterectomy; internal carotid artery tortuosity; posterior transverse plication; patch angioplasty; restenosis.

title: Radiological and radiomic outcomes following pressure-controlled fibrinolytic irrigation therapy for acute subdural hematoma.
abstract: Introduction The optimal management of neurologically stable acute subdural hematoma (aSDH) remains uncertain. Twist-drill-craniostomy with pressure-controlled-fibrinolytic irrigation (TDC-FIT) offers a minimally invasive approach, but its imaging effects remain poorly characterized. Research question To assess radiological, radiomic, and clinical outcomes after TDC-FIT. Material and methods This retrospective, single-center study included neurologically stable aSDH patients treated between July 2023 and June 2025. Pretreatment computed tomography (CT) scans and the first CT before irrigation discontinuation were assessed for hematoma volume, midline shift, attenuation in Hounsfield units (HU), skewness, and kurtosis. Paired nonparametric tests compared imaging measurements. Clinical outcomes, complications, and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores were recorded. Results Twenty-five patients were included (52% male; mean age, 83 years). Median hematoma volume decreased from 83.6 cm 3 (IQR 62.4-111.0) to 21.0 cm 3 (IQR 5.0-35.6; p < 0.0001), and midline shift from 6.0 to 0.0 mm (p = 0.00065). Median percentage volume reduction was 74.9% (IQR 63.3-93.1%). Mean intralesional attenuation decreased from a cohort median of 59.9 to 48.0 HU (p = 0.0025); skewness changed from -0.56 to -0.14 (p = 0.019). Median mRS was 2 premorbidly, 3 at discharge, and 2 at 3 months. Procedure-related complications comprised rebleeding requiring craniotomy in two patients (8%), symptomatic chronic SDH recurrence in two (8%), and device failure in one (4%). Both rebleeding scans preceded rescue craniotomy. Discussion and conclusion TDC-FIT was associated with hematoma reduction and changes in attenuation and skewness. These findings may reflect altered hematoma composition, but their biological significance remains uncertain. Prospective controlled studies are needed to establish safety and efficacy.

title: Usage and pitfalls of intracranial/invasive multimodal neuromonitoring during MR imaging of neurocritical care patients: a questionnaire study.
abstract: Introduction Invasive intracranial neuromonitoring and early magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) inform treatment and prognosis in traumatic brain injury (TBI), but probes in situ raise MRI safety concerns. Research question How do neurocritical care clinicians handle MRI in patients with intracranial neuromonitoring probes? Materials and methods A cross-sectional open online survey was distributed via European and international neurosurgical and neurocritical care networks. It covered demographics, probe placement and MRI practices. Data were analyzed descriptively with 95% confidence intervals and exploratory Fisher's exact tests. Results Ninety clinicians from 29 countries participated, predominantly neurosurgeons (85.6%) practicing in Europe (71/84, 84.5%). Frontal placement was reported by 97.1% (66/68) and ipsilateral placement by 67.2% (43/64). Probes were inserted in the operating room by 51.5% and at the bedside by 48.5%; 61.8% used bolt systems (n = 68). Of 87 respondents, 51.7% kept all probes in situ during MRI, 29.9% removed all and 18.4% removed selected probes. Respondents removing probes (n = 41) most often cited absent MRI safety testing (46.3%) and thermal injury (41.5%); of those leaving probes in situ (n = 57), 66.7% reported no complications. MRI was performed on demand by 54.0% and within seven days by 37.9% (n = 87). No respondent characteristic was significantly associated with these practices. Discussion and conclusion Respondents broadly agreed on frontal placement, whereas lateralization, insertion technique and MRI-related probe handling varied considerably. These self-reported data from a predominantly European, neurosurgical sample cannot establish MRI safety with probes in situ. Device-specific MRI safety testing, prospective multicenter registries and multidisciplinary consensus are needed to standardize practice.

title: Choroid plexus enlargement in unmedicated major depressive disorder inflammation, oxidative stress and treatment outcome.
abstract: Background The choroid plexus has emerged as a putative neuroimmune interface implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). Choroid plexus enlargement has been reported across several MDD cohorts, yet its relationship with peripheral inflammation, oxidative stress, and antidepressant treatment response remains unresolved. Methods We used data from NeuroPharm-1, an open-label trial of escitalopram in 96 unmedicated patients with moderate-to-severe MDD and 84 healthy controls (HC) aged 18 to 57 years. Choroid plexus volume (CPV) was measured using deep-learning-based segmentation of T1-weighted MRI. Peripheral inflammation was indexed by high-sensitivity C-Reactive Protein (hsCRP), and oxidative stress by urinary 8-oxodG and 8-oxoGuo. Group differences in CPV were examined using a general linear model controlling for age, sex, BMI, and total intracranial volume. Associations with inflammation, oxidative stress, and treatment effects over 12 weeks were assessed in secondary and exploratory analyses. Analyses were preregistered at AsPredicted.org (ID 270379) RESULTS: Patients showed larger CPV than HC (β = 194 mm3 [9, 378], p = 0.040; Hedges' g = 0.32). However, pretreatment CPV was not associated with depression severity (HAMD17), hsCRP, or oxidative stress. Pretreatment CPV did not predict symptom trajectory over 12 weeks. CPV remained stable from baseline to week 8, with no significant change (p = 0.452). Conclusions This study replicates CPV enlargement in unmedicated MDD, strengthening evidence that it is a feature of the disorder. CPV was unrelated to peripheral inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, suggesting cumulative blood-CSF barrier reactivity rather than concurrent circulating inflammation. CPV did not decrease with treatment, suggesting high short-term stability.

title: Regional radiomics similarity networks reveal specific brain morphological connectivity patterns in migraine and tension-type headaches.
abstract: Objective This study investigated structural brain alterations in migraine and tension-type headache using regional radiomics similarity network to characterize disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns. Background Migraine and tension-type headache are the most prevalent primary headache disorders involving central nervous system dysfunction. While functional magnetic resonance imaging has revealed abnormalities, structural changes remain incompletely understood. Regional radiomics similarity network, a novel approach for modeling individualized morphological brain networks, has not been applied in primary headaches. Methods We enrolled 65 migraine patients, 49 tension-type headache patients, and 53 healthy controls. Regional radiomics similarity network was constructed using 88 radiomics features. Regional mean connectivity strength and voxel-based morphometry were compared across groups. Spearman correlation was performed between network measures and visual analogue scale scores. Generative adversarial networks were used for classification. Results Voxel-based morphometry revealed gray matter volume alterations in cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions across the three groups. Regional radiomics similarity network analysis identified distinct morphological connectivity patterns: patients with migraine showed altered connectivity involving frontal, limbic, and subcortical regions, whereas patients with tension-type headache exhibited prominent alterations involving the cerebellum and thalamic-temporal connections. Exploratory partial correlation analyses suggested associations between several altered connections and pain severity. The model achieved 84.31% classification accuracy. Conclusions Regional radiomics similarity network captures disease-specific morphological connectivity patterns beyond conventional structural measurements, providing insights into structural network substrates of primary headaches. This study establishes regional radiomics similarity network as a promising neuroimaging framework for investigating brain structural alterations in migraine and tension-type headache.

title: Towards precision oncology in pancreatic cancer: Diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers from conventional methods to liquid biopsy and artificial intelligence-based approaches.
abstract: Pancreatic cancer (PC) is known as one of the most aggressive and deadly tumors, with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) predicted to be the second leading cause of cancer death by 2030. Also, due to the lack of specific symptoms and limitations of biomarkers and screening methods for early diagnosis, most patients are diagnosed at advanced stages and with metastatic disease. Therefore, developing new, high-accuracy diagnostic methods for early diagnosis and monitoring of treatment response in patients is very important for providing appropriate treatment options and improving survival rates. In recent years, despite the progress in diagnostic methods such as imaging techniques, tissue biopsy, liquid biopsy (LB), and tumor marker testing, there are many uncertainties about the specificity and sensitivity of these technologies, as well as challenges in their practical use in the clinic. Also, advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the field of cancer detection have enabled the screening and early diagnosis of PC in high-risk populations by employing AI algorithms with high computational power in conjunction with biomarkers, medical imaging, and pathological tests. In this article, we comprehensively evaluate the potential and diagnostic effectiveness of established tools for PC, alongside emerging and promising approaches, including liquid biopsy and AI-based methods. We examine their applications in early diagnosis, screening, prognostication, and disease monitoring, while also discussing the key characteristics, advantages, and limitations of each approach, as well as the potential benefits of their integration. Finally, we provide clinical recommendations aimed at improving the early detection of this challenging disease.

title: Cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis mediates DIZE-induced inhibition of TGF-β signaling to attenuate cardiac fibrosis following myocardial infarction.
abstract: Cardiac fibrosis represents a critical pathological determinant of poor prognosis in coronary artery disease (CAD). Pharmacological activation of the angiotensin-Converting enzyme 2/angiotensin-(1-7) (ACE2/Ang-(1-7)) axis is a promising anti-fibrotic approach for cardiac fibrosis, a condition that currently lacks effective therapies. Diminazene aceturate (DIZE) is recognized as an ACE2 agonist with anti‑fibrotic activity, the molecular mechanism of which has not been fully elucidated. This study demonstrates that the anti-fibrotic effects of DIZE are exerted via a cardiomyocyte-mediated paracrine mechanism, rather than through direct action on fibroblasts. Using a cardiomyocyte-fibroblast co-culture system and transcriptomic analysis, we found that ACE2 activated by DIZE on cardiomyocytes enhances the conversion of Ang II to Ang-(1-7), which subsequently suppresses the pro-fibrotic transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling in adjacent fibroblasts. This effect was partially abrogated by the Ang-(1-7) antagonist A779, confirming Ang-(1-7) as a key paracrine mediator. To exploit this mechanism in vivo, a collagen-binding, low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU)-responsive nanoplatform (CNA35-GDP) was developed for specific DIZE delivery. In a rat model of myocardial infarction, LIFU-triggered DIZE release from CNA35-GDP was found to significantly improve cardiac function and attenuate fibrosis. These therapeutic benefits were accompanied by restoration of the ACE2/Ang-(1-7) axis and suppression of TGF-β signaling, thereby validating the proposed mechanism. Collectively, activation of cardiomyocyte-derived ACE2 by DIZE inhibits collagen production in fibroblasts through paracrine Ang-(1-7) and downstream suppression of TGF‑β signaling.

title: Balancing mechanical stability and biological performance through a dual-setting approach in granular silicate-CPCs.
abstract: Granular bone substitute systems are widely used to treat complex and irregular defects due to their adaptability and prefabricated nature, which eliminates in situ setting-related instability. However, their limited mechanical stability makes their performance highly dependent on intraoperative handling and increases the risk of impaired tissue ingrowth. In this study, granular brushite- and monetite-based calcium phosphate cements (CPCs) were developed and systematically investigated to improve mechanical performance and cytocompatibility through a dual-setting approach. Silicate-based precursors, specifically tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) and 1,8-bis(triethoxysilyl)octane (BTESO), were incorporated into the CPC formulation prior to granulation to establish a reinforcing secondary network within the cement matrix. Structural and mechanical properties were assessed, including compression-induced changes, which were analysed using micro-computed tomography (μCT). The biocompatibility of the CPCs was further investigated using WST assays, cell counting, DNA quantification, and scanning electron microscope with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX). The incorporation of TEOS significantly increased mechanical stability and cytocompatibility compared to conventional formulations. TEOS-modified granules exhibited less than one-third of the compression-induced deformation observed for the control, which showed a height reduction of more than 5 mm. μCT analysis further revealed a shift in the intergranular pore-size peak from approximately 350 to 250 μm after compression in the control, whereas no apparent shift was observed for TEOS-modified granules. Granule size itself affected intergranular pore geometry, with larger granules showing higher metabolic activity. TEOS-modified granules showed the most favourable overall biological response, whereas the addition of BTESO provided no further mechanical or biological benefit. Furthermore, a cryosectioning approach enabled fluorescence imaging of osteoblast-like cells on CPCs with high autofluorescence, allowing visualisation of cell morphology on the material surface. Overall, the dual-setting approach, particularly using TEOS, improved resistance to compression while preserving intergranular pore architecture and maintaining favourable cytocompatibility, thereby addressing a key limitation of granular CPC-based bone substitute systems. In parallel, cryosectioning enables reliable fluorescence-based visualisation of cells on highly autofluorescent materials, offering a practical approach for the biological assessment of such systems.

title: Molecular Biomarkers and Biosensing Innovations for the Early Diagnosis of Ankylosing Spondylitis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Diagnostics.
abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis is a chronic immune-mediated, inflammatory spondyloarthropathy in which delayed diagnosis remains a major clinical challenge, particularly during the early stages when definitive structural radiographic changes may be absent. Although HLA-B27 represents the most potent genetic association with ankylosing spondylitis, its incomplete penetrance and variability limit its use as a single diagnostic biomarker. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms underlying HLA-B27-associated disease, evaluates circulating and molecular biomarkers according to their demonstrated clinical roles and assesses the current development of biosensing technologies for their detection. Biomarkers including IL-17, IL-13, TNF-α, MMP-3, calprotectin, microRNAs, and anti-CD74 antibodies reflect complementary aspects of inflammation, immune dysregulation and tissue remodelling; however, their biological association with the disease should not be compared with validated early diagnostic performance. Emerging optical and electrochemical biosensing platforms demonstrate promising analytical sensitivity and potential for rapid and minimally invasive detection. However, much of the available biosensor research remains at the level of analytical feasibility or biomarker detection, with limited evidence demonstrating discrimination of ankylosing spondylitis from clinical controls and very limited independent clinical validation. Major translational barriers include biomarker heterogeneity, sensor standardisation, and clinical testing. Future development should focus on clinically validated multi-biomarker biosensor systems, nanomaterial-enhanced detection and machine learning-assisted analysis. Collectively, the combination of molecular biomarker research and next-generation biosensing technology can elevate diagnostic accuracy, providing early intervention and precision medicine strategies for disease assessment.

title: A sequentially verified dual-lock near-infrared fluorescent probe for imaging lysosomal H 2 O 2 /microviscosity dynamics during radiotherapy and STING agonist sensitization.
abstract: Low-dose fractionated radiotherapy is widely used to limit normal tissue damage, yet repeated low-dose irradiation can remodel the tumour microenvironment in ways that impair antitumour immunity and reduce radioimmunotherapy efficacy. Importantly, this immunological outcome coincides with dynamic inflammatory reprogramming at cellular and subcellular levels. Inflammatory status thus provides a mechanistic link between radiotherapy-induced microenvironmental changes and treatment efficacy, but real-time tools to track these fluctuations are still scarce. Here we present Lyso-SCMU-H 2 O 2 , a lysosome-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe for high-fidelity imaging of therapy-related inflammatory dynamics via a dual-lock AND logic gate responsive to H 2 O 2 and microviscosity. In this design, H 2 O 2 -induced boronate cleavage relieves photoinduced electron transfer (PeT) quenching, and high viscosity subsequently inhibits twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) decay, enabling excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) to produce a large-Stokes-shift NIR signal. This ordered dual validation reduces false positives and improves signal clarity in complex biological settings. Spectroscopic and cellular assays confirmed the stringent dual-lock mechanism, precise lysosomal localisation, and strong response to endogenous inflammatory activation. Using this platform, we observed that repeated 2 Gy irradiation progressively weakened lysosomal inflammatory signalling, and after five fractions, tumour-cell survival increased significantly. In contrast, adding the STING agonist MSA-2 restored the inflammatory fluorescence response and markedly enhanced antitumour efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. These results establish Lyso-SCMU-H 2 O 2 as a high-contrast molecular imaging tool for linking radiotherapy-induced inflammatory remodelling to immune-related outcomes and for guiding more effective radioimmunotherapy strategies.

title: Revisiting the role of fluorescent dyes in the detection of amorphous and amyloid aggregates: The quest continues.
abstract: Protein aggregation is a hallmark of various neurodegenerative and systemic disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and type 2 diabetes. The ability to detect and characterize aggregates in both in vitro and in vivo systems is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and developing diagnostic strategies. Fluorescent dyes have emerged as powerful tools for probing protein aggregates, offering insights into their structural variations and formation pathways. This review provides a comprehensive comparison of classical and emerging fluorescent dyes. It correlates their binding specificity and performance metrics, including quantum yield, fluorescence enhancement, and binding affinity, with molecular recognition mechanisms such as TICT restriction, π-π stacking, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic interactions. We categorize the dyes based on their blood-brain barrier (BBB) crossing ability, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging suitability, environmental sensitivity, nucleic acid binding affinity, luminescent conjugated oligothiophenes (LCOs), and nanoparticle-conjugation. We also consider their applicability to in vitro, in vivo and ex vivo settings, highlighting their use in detecting different aggregate species. We further assess dye suitability for amyloid versus amorphous aggregates and for different experimental contexts, considering critical parameters. By bridging structural features with functional outcomes, this review offers guidance for probe selection and highlights future directions for rational dye design to enhance sensitivity and selectivity in aggregate detection.

title: Hypoxia-primed human adipose-derived stem cell secretome accelerates gastric ulcer healing and promotes tissue remodeling in a murine model.
abstract: Background The secretome of adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs), collected as conditioned medium (CM), has shown potential as a cell-free approach for gastrointestinal mucosal repair. However, standard normoxic culture produces a basal secretome that may be insufficient to achieve high-quality mucosal regeneration in severe lesions. Although microenvironmental preconditioning can enrich the secretome, in vivo evidence comparing how distinct stressors, specifically hypoxia and oxidative stress, differentially influence the structural and molecular features of gastric ulcer healing at a single repair stage remains limited. Objective To compare the therapeutic efficacy and morphomolecular profiles of concentrated CM derived from human ADSCs cultured under standard normoxia (Nor-CM), hypoxia (Hypo-CM), and sublethal oxidative stress (H 2 O 2 -CM) in a murine model of acetic acid-induced chronic gastric ulcer at Day 7 after induction. Methods Following in vitro preconditioning and concentration, the secretomes were administered intragastrically to mice for 6 consecutive days. Repair parameters were evaluated on Day 7 using systemic body weight recovery, macroscopic morphometry, phenotypic histopathology (H&E), functional restitution of the mucosal barrier (PAS), and transcriptional profiling of apoptotic, inflammatory, and pro-regenerative networks. Cohen's d effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were reported alongside hypothesis testing to quantify the magnitude of biological effects in the context of inherent in vivo variability. Results Hypoxic preconditioning enhanced secretome yield and in vivo therapeutic performance. Hypo-CM showed a strong trend toward accelerated systemic weight recovery (11.35 ± 5.70% vs. Sham, 4.45 ± 9.50%; p = 0.195, d = 0.88, 95% CI [-0.04, 1.80]) and produced the highest incidence of complete macroscopic re-epithelialization (3/10, 30%), although the difference in incidence was not significant ( p = 0.582 vs. Sham, 1/10). Histologically, healed Hypo-CM specimens uniquely showed restoration of a continuous, surface-localized mucin layer, in contrast to the reactive mucin accumulation within deep glands observed with unprimed treatment. At the molecular level, Hypo-CM was associated with a favorable immunomodulatory and structural profile on Day 7, with attenuation of pro-inflammatory signaling ( IL-6 , d = 0.43; TNF-α , d = 0.54) and marked downregulation of hepatocyte growth factor ( HGF , d = 0.87 vs. Sham). This reduction in HGF expression on Day 7, together with histological re-epithelialization, was consistent with a transition from active cellular proliferation to mucosal remodeling. In contrast, H 2 O 2 -CM showed moderate structural efficacy but maintained an altered inflammatory profile, with suppressed TNF-α and elevated IL-6 ( d = 0.50), accompanied by persistent cystic glandular dilation. Nor-CM showed the weakest overall efficacy, with tissues remaining in an incompletely repaired, HGF -elevated state. Conclusion The in vitro preconditioning microenvironment markedly influences the functional efficacy of the ADSC secretome on Day 7 after ulcer induction. Hypoxic preconditioning enhances secretome potency, promotes resolution of acute inflammatory gene expression, and supports structural tissue remodeling and restoration of the mucosal barrier during chronic gastric ulcer repair.

title: Planning and insetting strategies to optimize outcomes in PAP flap breast reconstruction.
abstract: The profunda artery perforator (PAP) flap has become an established alternative for autologous breast reconstruction when abdominal tissue is inadequate or undesirable. Here, we aimed to describe our institutional experience by focusing on preoperative perforator mapping, flap design, and insetting strategies. A retrospective review was conducted by including all consecutive PAP flap reconstructions performed between 2016 and 2025. Sixteen patients underwent 22 flaps, including 5 bilateral and 1 stacked-flap case; 63.6% were delayed reconstructions. Preoperative colour Doppler ultrasonography was used to identify dominant perforators with complete concordance to intraoperative findings (100%), thereby supporting its use as a radiation-free alternative to computed tomography angiography. All flaps were designed with a horizontal skin paddle, and the mean diameter of the dominant perforator was 1.17 mm. The perforator was located within the skin paddle in 6 flaps (27.3%) and incorporated through beveling of the adipofascial component in 16 flaps (72.7%). Intraoperative indocyanine-green angiography confirmed adequate perfusion in all cases. Complete flap survival was achieved (100%), with no perfusion-related or donor-site complications. Internal mammary vessels were used as recipients in 95.5% of the cases. This series illustrates the feasibility of the described planning and insetting strategies in selected patients. The proposed algorithm integrates flap laterality, beveling, rotation, and pedicle orientation; however, its reproducibility and effect on clinical outcomes require further evaluation. LAY SUMMARY: We describe an approach to reconstruct breasts using the PAP flap, focusing on how the tissue and its blood vessels are positioned according to the skin and volume required. The approach is based on our clinical experience and requires further evaluation.

title: Paired DXA and pQCT of bone parameters in a clinical paediatric population: A cluster analysis.
abstract: Accurate assessment of bone health in paediatric clinical populations is needed for the prevention of both non-specific and condition-specific bone deficits. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), particularly "total body less head" (TBLH), is the preferred clinical measurement. However, peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) provides additional structural insights of value to a paediatric population. Criteria are needed to establish the value of pQCT beyond use in research settings. To determine the contributions of pQCT and DXA, we analysed data from 457 individuals from a Western Australian paediatric centre routinely employing joint DXA-pQCT imaging. Sex-specific cluster analysis was performed utilising DXA-TBLH BMD, pQCT (4% and 66% arm and leg volumetric density), age and height to define clinical phenotypes and guide decision making on adding pQCT to BMD analyses. Results showed DXA and pQCT measurements were positively correlated, particularly at the 4% site. Cluster analysis showed two clusters with lower bone density and higher fracture frequency characterised by malabsorption and bone mineral metabolism conditions in females, and bone mineral metabolism and neuromuscular conditions in males. DXA and pQCT variation was greatest in these clusters, with DXA being lower. Females showed greater variability between DXA and pQCT, with height as an influencing factor. These findings reinforce the utility of combined DXA and pQCT in paediatric bone health assessment particularly in high-risk groups.

title: Gynecologic hybrid and interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy.
abstract: Advances in high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy techniques have improved local control and reduced morbidities associated with brachytherapy. Interstitial brachytherapy (ISBT) has traditionally been used for locally advanced gynecologic cancers not amenable to less invasive intracavitary brachytherapy (ICBT) techniques. The recent advent of hybrid brachytherapy (HBT) involves using modern brachytherapy applicators that combine intracavitary and interstitial components to optimize tumor target coverage and reduce normal tissue exposure. Given the importance of brachytherapy in the non-operative management of locally advanced gynecologic cancers, knowledge of and procedural competency with ISBT and HBT is crucial. However, gynecologic brachytherapy training during radiation oncology residency is variable, with significant gaps in experience and case numbers reported by resident trainees. The advent of HBT and ISBT may further exacerbate these gaps, as not all centers are equipped to provide training in high-quality HBT and ISBT. To this end, this article aims to summarize important concepts in ISBT and HBT, with a focus on cervical cancer, and to describe brachytherapy applicators, aspects of procedural competency, target delineation, treatment planning, and toxicity management.

title: A systematic review of barriers to mammography screening and timely breast cancer diagnosis and treatment initiation: estimating the global impact.
abstract: Importance Breast cancer (BC) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women and a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Understanding and addressing the barriers women face in accessing BC care is crucial for improving clinical outcomes and public health. Objective This paper describes and discusses the findings from a systematic literature review (SLR) of the barriers that women worldwide face in accessing mammography screening and diagnosis, which may lead to delays in BC treatment. We also aimed to estimate the number of women worldwide affected by delayed or absent. We also aimed to estimate the number of women affected by delayed or absent access to medical services. Evidence review The systematic literature review included a comprehensive search in bibliographic databases and grey literature. A total of 20,434 citations were identified, with 2,611 citations eligible for full-text examination, which resulted in 256 extracted sources fulfilling the inclusion criteria. We focused on quantitative data on the number of patients whose access to BC-related medical services was hindered by such barriers. Findings The review identified education, age, and geographic region as important factors influencing barriers to mammography. Educational level, residential location, and travel time showed the strongest associations with delay in BC diagnosis. Socio-demographic characteristics also had an impact on the stage of cancer at diagnosis. An estimated 869.8 million women are aged 50-75 years worldwide. Of these, approximately 679.7 million women (78%) do not receive mammography because either their country has no established mammography program (557.7 million) or because existing programs have low uptake rates for various reasons (122.1 million). Of the 2.3 million new BC cases annually worldwide, approximately 796,000 women may experience delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation. In an exploratory, scenario-based approximation, nearly 127,000 deaths each year could be associated with delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation due to more advanced disease presentation and postponed interventions. Conclusions and relevance These findings highlight the challenges women face in accessing mammography programs and the large number of women living in regions without mammography coverage (e.g., due to socioeconomic status or distance to a mammography center). They underscore the urgent need for the WHO Global Breast Cancer Initiative, which aims to establish early detection programs to promote earlier diagnosis and reduce BC mortality, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

title: A Spatial Multi-omics Atlas of Intra- and Extrapancreatic Perineural Invasion Reveals Basal-like Neurotropism and Stromal Remodeling in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a prominent feature of pancreatic cancer (PDAC) and is closely associated with tumor progression and poor prognosis. However, its spatial cellular architecture and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we applied high-resolution spatial transcriptomics to construct a comprehensive atlas of the PNI microenvironment across distinct anatomical regions of intra and extra-pancreas. We observed that the Basal-like tumor subtype exhibited a higher propensity for PNI compared with the Classical subtype, a finding further supported by multiplex imaging on whole-mount histopathology. Comparative spatial analysis revealed distinct immune and stromal organization between tumor subtypes, with enrichment of M2-like macrophage potentially promoting epithelial cell migration in the vicinity of Basal-like tumors. In addition, we identified myofibroblast subset may promote Schwann cell activation and PNI-associated nerve injury was further accompanied by a shift toward inflammatory fibroblast polarization and features of CD8 + T cell exhaustion within the local microenvironment. Finally, spatial profiling indicated functional heterogeneity among tumor-associated Schwann cells, which may contribute to the tumor progression. Collectively, this study provides a spatially resolved view of the cellular and molecular landscape of PNI in PDAC and offers insights into Basal-specific neurotropic behavior and microenvironmental reorganization.

title: Intrafraction organs-at-risk volume and dose variations in upper abdominal adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy on 0.35 T magnetic resonance-guided linear accelerator.
abstract: Background Magnetic resonance-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy allows daily adaptive planning to account for anatomical variations. However, anatomical changes may still occur during treatment delivery. This study assessed intrafraction organ-at-risk mobility by comparing magnetic resonance images acquired at the beginning and end of each fraction on a 0.35 T magnetic resonance-guided linear accelerator, in order to evaluate intrafraction anatomical and dosimetric variations. Methods Twenty upper abdominal lesions (liver, adrenal glands, pancreas, and lymph nodes) were treated with interfraction adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy delivered in five fractions using a stereotactic magnetic resonance-guided online adaptive radiotherapy protocol. For each fraction, organs at risk within a 3-cm isotropic margin around the planning target volume were delineated offline on both beginning- and end-of-fraction magnetic resonance images. Treatments were delivered under fasting conditions, without intrafraction plan reoptimization. The stomach, duodenum, small bowel, and colon were analyzed. Volume and dose variations were assessed using absolute differences and rates of variation. Results The largest volume variations were observed for the small bowel and colon, with median variation rates of 27.7 and 30.9 %, respectively. Stomach and duodenum volumes decreased during treatment, whereas the small bowel showed a median increase of 21 %, corresponding to a median absolute increase of 1.8cm 3 . Small bowel dose parameters increased, with a maximum dose rise of 1.5Gy, while most stomach and duodenal dose metrics decreased. Conclusions Intrafraction anatomical changes resulted in measurable organ-at-risk dose variations, highlighting a potential source of dosimetric uncertainty during magnetic resonance-guided adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy.

Twenty upper abdominal lesions (liver, adrenal glands, pancreas, and lymph nodes) were treated with interfraction adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy delivered in five fractions using a stereotactic magnetic resonance-guided online adaptive radiotherapy protocol. For each fraction, organs at risk within a 3-cm isotropic margin around the planning target volume were delineated offline on both beginning- and end-of-fraction magnetic resonance images. Treatments were delivered under fasting conditions, without intrafraction plan reoptimization. The stomach, duodenum, small bowel, and colon were analyzed. The largest volume variations were observed for the small bowel and colon, with median variation rates of 27.7 and 30.9 %, respectively. title: Patterns of recurrence after stereotactic ablative radiotherapy for hepatocellular carcinoma: A monocentric retrospective analysis.
abstract: Introduction Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy is an option for the treatment of early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma. However, there is a scarcity of data investigating hepatic recurrence patterns, i.e. the location of recurrences in relation to radiation fields. The purpose of this study, was to characterise intrahepatic recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma after stereotactic ablative radiotherapy, and to report survival outcomes and treatment tolerance. Materials and methods We included patients with one to two unresectable, localised hepatocellular carcinoma lesions who were not eligible for percutaneous ablation, with Child-Pugh class A to B7 liver function and performance status up to 2 according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group. Hepatic recurrences were analyzed by fusing the planning computed tomography with recurrence imaging to study the relationship between the planning target volume and the recurrence centroid. Local recurrence was defined as "in-field" if the centroid touched or crossed the planning target volume, "marginal" if within up to 1 cm, or "out-of-field" otherwise. Secondary endpoints included hepatic progression-free-survival, overall survival, risk factors for progression-free survival, and toxicity. Results Between 2016 and 2023, 64 consecutive patients (70 lesions) were treated with a median dose of 45Gy in three fractions to the 80 % isodose line. Forty-eight patients had received prior local treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma, and 32 had received treatment of the irradiated nodule. Over a median follow-up of 28 months, the intrahepatic recurrence rate was 40.6 %, with 80.9 % occurring out-of-field, 19.2 % marginal, and none in-field. The median hepatic progression-free survival was 14 months (95 % confidence interval: 1-26 months), and the median overall survival was 33 months (95 % confidence interval: 5-42 months). No progression-free survival risk factors were identified. Conclusion Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy provides excellent in-field local control for localized hepatocellular carcinoma. Future studies should harmonise intrahepatic control definitions using field-based approaches.

title: Prediction of Liver Histology Response by Non-Invasive Tests: Exploratory Analysis of the Survodutide Phase 2 Trial.
abstract: Current guidelines recommend using non-invasive tests (NITs) for the diagnosis, monitoring, and prognosis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). This post-hoc analysis in 295 participants with F1-F3 fibrosis, randomized to placebo or survodutide 2.4/4.8/6.0 mg assessed changes in NITs from baseline to week 48. An analysis in participants with F2-F3 (n=118) assessed whether percentage change in FAST, Agile 3+, ALT, body weight, MRI-PDFF, liver stiffness (VCTE™), PRO-C3, and absolute change in ELF™ had predictive potential for 2 biopsy-based outcomes: resolution of MASH with no worsening of fibrosis, and improvement of fibrosis with no worsening of MASH using AUC, 95% CI and a corresponding P-value. Models included changes in NITs (dichotomized by Youden index) chosen by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator with 3-fold cross-validation. Participants who received survodutide had improvements in all assessed NITs vs placebo. Changes in MRI-PDFF (relative importance to the prediction: 100%), ELF™ (61.9%), and FAST score (50.4%) were predictive of resolution of MASH with no worsening of fibrosis (full dataset: AUC 0.85, 95% CI, 0.78-0.93, P<.0001; AUC based on cross-validation: 0.84). Changes in ELF™ (100%), ALT (87.2%), PRO-C3 (76.3%), MRI-PDFF (75.6%), FAST score (72.3%), Agile 3+ (50.5%), and CAP™ (13.6%) were predictive of improvement of fibrosis with no worsening of MASH (full dataset: AUC 0.81, 95% CI, 0.73-0.90, P<.0001; AUC based on cross-validation: 0.76). Changes in MRI-PDFF, ELF™ score, and FAST score were identified as the most important for prediction of the 2 biopsy outcomes. Larger datasets are needed to enhance model accuracy and refinement.

title: Effect of soft contact lens correction on quantitative OCT and OCT angiography measurements in high myopia: A prospective paired study.
abstract: Purpose To determine whether soft contact lens correction alters quantitative optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), macular optical coherence tomography (OCT), and optic nerve head measurements in highly myopic eyes. Methods Twenty patients with cycloplegic spherical refraction of -6.00 D or more myopic underwent swept-source OCT/OCTA with the DRI OCT Triton 3D Plus. Macular 6 × 6-mm and optic disc scans were acquired first without a contact lens using internal refractive compensation and then repeated through an ACUVUE OASYS spherical soft contact lens. SCP and DCP vessel density, image quality, macular structural variables, optic disc morphometry, and sectoral RNFL thickness were compared using participant-level paired change scores. False discovery rate (FDR) was controlled with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results Thirty-eight eyes of 20 patients were analyzed (mean age 26.95 ± 6.32 years; mean spherical refraction -7.49 ± 1.48 D). Contact lens correction reduced OCTA quality and SCP vessel density in the central, superior, temporal, and nasal regions (all FDR-adjusted q < 0.05). Central DCP vessel density decreased, whereas inferior DCP vessel density increased. Retinal thickness decreased modestly, inferior RNFL thickness increased, and optic disc quality decreased; most global structural parameters remained stable. Conclusions Soft contact lens correction systematically influenced selected quantitative OCT/OCTA measurements in high myopia. The concurrent reduction in scan quality and several vessel-density measurements suggests an important optical or acquisition-related component. Longitudinal OCT/OCTA examinations should therefore use a consistent refractive correction condition.

title: Postoperative midline shift and functional outcome after surgery for chronic subdural hematoma.
abstract: Background Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) lacks well-established postoperative radiological markers associated with long-term functional outcome. We evaluated the association between postoperative midline shift (MLS) and 6-month functional outcome using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after CSDH surgery. Methods We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from 172 surgical CSDH patients. The primary prognostic analysis was restricted to unilateral CSDH (n=122) because opposing mass effects alter MLS interpretation in bilateral hematomas. The primary outcome was unfavorable 6-month functional status (mRS 3-6). A parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression model adjusting for age, admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), and postoperative MLS (modeled continuously first, and as ≥5 vs. <5 mm secondarily) was fitted. Results Among 122 unilateral CSDH patients, 22 (18.0%) had an unfavorable 6-month outcome. Across 106 re-evaluated postoperative CT scans, intraobserver and interobserver reliability was excellent for continuous MLS (ICC: 0.982 and 0.985) and high for the ≥5-mm threshold (κ: 0.902 and 0.862). In the primary Firth model, continuous postoperative MLS showed a positive but imprecisely estimated association with unfavorable outcome (OR 1.16 per 1-mm increase, 95% CI 0.983-1.36; p=0.079), with an apparent c-statistic of 0.704 (95% CI 0.564-0.844) and bootstrap optimism-corrected c-statistic of 0.674. In the secondary model, postoperative MLS ≥5 mm was associated with higher odds of unfavorable outcome (OR 2.73, 95% CI 1.003-7.45; p=0.049). Conclusions Higher postoperative MLS showed a consistent direction of association with unfavorable 6-month outcome in unilateral CSDH, although the continuous estimate was imprecise. These findings support postoperative MLS as a potential prognostic marker rather than a therapeutic target, though its incremental prognostic value beyond pre-morbid functional status and preoperative radiological severity remains unknown. The 5-mm threshold does not justify imaging-driven reintervention.

title: Volumetric modeling of residual meningioma growth.
abstract: Purpose Meningioma resection remains incomplete in roughly 25% of cases; improved characterization of remnant growth could help clinicians optimize postoperative management. This study aims to characterize the volumetric growth of residual meningiomas and to identify factors associated with rapid growth. Methods A retrospective cohort design was applied to adult patients with residual WHO grade 1 intracranial meningioma. Tumor volume was measured at every postoperative MRI. Tumor growth rates (TGR) were derived and clustered. Factors associated with rapid growth were explored. Fit was compared across linear, exponential, Gompertzian and power models. Model performance on untrained datapoints was assessed. Results Sixty-one (61) remnants were followed for an average of 71.1 months (SD = 41.3) postoperatively. Mean TGR was 1.79 %/month (SD = 3.51) preoperatively and 1.68 %/month (SD = 4.36) postoperatively. The fast growth cluster represented 32% of the cohort with a mean TGR of 2.71 %/month (SD = 0.93) while the slow growth cluster represented 68% of the cohort with a mean TGR of 0.20 %/month (SD = 0.70) (p < 0.001). A positive correlation was found between preoperative and postoperative TGRs (ρ= 0.713, p < 0.001). Linear and exponential models best described growth. Prediction error on untrained datapoints grew over time. Conclusion Most meningioma remnants showed slow volumetric progression, whereas approximately one-third demonstrated rapid growth. Interestingly, postoperative growth rate may be linked to preoperative growth rate. Different growth models seem to offer comparable explanatory performance, with the accuracy of predictive models remaining limited.

title: Emphysematous osteomyelitis of the lower extremity: Prevalence, imaging features, interobserver agreement and clinical outcomes in a 16-hospital cohort.
abstract: Purpose To estimate emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) observed prevalence, compare 3-month major adverse events (death or major amputation) between EO and nonemphysematous osteomyelitis (NEO), and assess interobserver agreement for key imaging features. Methods In this retrospective 16-hospital study, radiology-report text screening followed by manual report review identified CT and MRI examinations demonstrating lower-extremity osteomyelitis. EO was defined as intraosseous gas without direct bone-to-air communication. Forty-five EO cases met criteria, and 180 NEO cases were randomly sampled in a 4:1 ratio for prognostic comparison. Associations with 3-month major adverse events were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Three radiologists independently reviewed 90 cases (45 EO, 45 NEO) to assess interobserver agreement. Results Of the 1417 imaging examinations that identified lower-extremity osteomyelitis, 45 (3.2%) met the study's EO inclusion criteria. Major adverse events occurred within 3 months in 33.3% (15/45) of EO cases and 12.8% (23/180) of nonemphysematous osteomyelitis cases. EO (adjusted OR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.46-7.12; p = .004) and peripheral artery disease (adjusted OR, 3.11; 95% CI, 1.38-7.03; p = .006) were independently associated with higher odds of death or major amputation within 3 months. Agreement for intraosseous gas was substantial on CT (κ = 0.71) and almost perfect on MRI (κ = 0.81). Conclusion EO is uncommon but associated with worse 3-month outcomes. Our findings support consideration of EO as a potential imaging marker of short-term adverse outcomes in patients with lower-extremity osteomyelitis.
