We found no clear evidence of an independent association between abscess cavities ≥6 cm and treatment failure or mortality after adjustment. Antibiotic therapy remains a valid initial approach, and intervention should be guided by clinical characteristics and response.

title: Feasibility of Intraoperative Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Angiography for Perfusion Assessment in Pediatric Adnexal Mass-Associated Torsion.
abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography for perfusion assessment in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion and to explore its potential clinical value using a historical comparison cohort. Retrospective cohort study with a historical comparison cohort. A single tertiary pediatric surgical center. Thirty-eight children who underwent surgery with intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography for adnexal mass-associated torsion between January 2022 and September 2024 were retrospectively compared with a historical cohort of 58 children treated without ICG between January 2020 and January 2022. Serial ICG fluorescence angiography was performed before detorsion and after lesion enucleation with adnexal reconstruction. Qualitative perfusion patterns, signal-to-background ratio (SBR), postoperative ultrasound findings, and propensity score-matched clinical outcomes were evaluated. All 38 patients successfully underwent intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography, with no ICG-related adverse events observed. Qualitative perfusion patterns changed from Type A/B/C in 3/16/19 patients before detorsion to 13/17/8 after adnexal reconstruction. The median signal-to-background ratio (SBR) increased from 0.841 (interquartile range [IQR], 0.569-0.979) before detorsion to 0.920 (IQR, 0.696-1.046) after reconstruction (P = .038). Among 16 patients with absent preoperative Doppler flow on the torsed side, 12 demonstrated Type A or B perfusion after reconstruction. Among the 36 patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound follow-up, 33 (91.7%) had a Good outcome, 2 (5.6%) had an Intermediate outcome, and 1 (2.8%) had a Poor outcome. Given the small numbers of Intermediate and Poor outcomes, associations between intraoperative ICG findings and postoperative ultrasound outcomes were evaluated descriptively. After 1:1 propensity score matching of patients with at least 3 months of postoperative ultrasound follow-up, 17 matched pairs were analyzed. Organ preservation was achieved in all patients in both groups (100% vs 100%; P = 1.000). Good postoperative ultrasound outcomes were observed in 17 of 17 patients (100%) in the ICG group and 16 of 17 patients (94.1%) in the non-ICG group, with no significant difference in outcome distribution (P = 1.000). Intraoperative ICG fluorescence angiography is a feasible adjunct for real-time perfusion assessment during organ-preserving surgery in children with adnexal mass-associated torsion. It provides additional information on tissue perfusion that may support intraoperative organ-preserving decision-making. Further prospective multicenter studies are warranted to establish its role in clinical practice.

title: Evaluation of knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of interventional radiology among the Jordanian population.
abstract: Background Interventional Radiology (IR) comprises multiple minimally invasive techniques that aid in the diagnosis and treatment of a plethora of conditions. However, some studies worldwide indicate low public awareness, with IR often conflated with Diagnostic Radiology (DR). No prior study has evaluated this knowledge gap in Jordan. This study aims to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of IR among the Jordanian population. Methods A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based survey was distributed via social media and convenience sampling. The survey, available in both English and Arabic, assessed demographics, awareness, procedural knowledge, and attitudes toward IR. A total of 429 participants were analyzed using R software. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multivariable logistic regression. Results Slightly over half (52.2%) of participants had heard of IR. Self-assessed knowledge was low (67.6% "Poor/Very poor"), and 73.9% were confused about the difference between IR and DR. While 72.0% preferred IR over surgery in a hypothetical choice, only 44.1% definitively agreed to undergo an IR procedure when advised. Awareness was significantly lower among females and those in non-medical occupations. High rates of misattribution were observed, with only 18.2% correctly identifying MRI as a DR procedure. Conclusion There is a significant public knowledge gap regarding IR in Jordan, creating an "awareness-preference paradox." Despite a theoretical preference for minimally invasive IR treatments, a lack of concrete knowledge hinders real-world acceptance. Targeted educational initiatives are needed to clarify the role of IR and improve the utilization of these therapeutic options. Plain language summary Interventional radiology uses minimally invasive procedures guided by medical imaging and can offer an alternative to some types of surgery. This study surveyed people in Jordan to understand their knowledge and views of interventional radiology and related imaging services. This study found that awareness and understanding of interventional radiology were generally low, many people confused it with diagnostic imaging, but most said they would prefer a minimally invasive treatment option. This matters because better public education could help people make informed healthcare decisions and improve access to available treatment options.

title: A reproducible pipeline for simulating individual and inter-brain neural dynamics from structural connectivity.
abstract: Background Computational models can link anatomical structure to neural dynamics. However, there is no validated, reproducible pipeline that simulates individual and inter-brain EEG-like dynamics from an individual's own structural connectome. New method To address this, we developed a comprehensive computational pipeline that combines probabilistic tractography from Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI) with dynamical systems modeling to simulate EEG-like neural dynamics from individual connectomes. It extracts anatomical connectivity, intra-individual functional connectivity, and inter-individual (two-brain) functional coupling features. It then evaluates their group-discriminative information with random-forest classification under repeated nested cross-validation. Simulated phase-locking values are calibrated against empirical resting-state EEG. Results In a test sample of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and matched controls (16 each), simulated intra-individual synchrony added classification information beyond anatomy, raising accuracy from 71.2% (AUC 0.843) to 77.6% (AUC 0.871), in a sample where groups did not differ in mean structural connectivity. Comparison with existing methods Unlike current single-brain simulations, this pipeline generates and jointly simulates two individual brain models within a single system, and reports the contribution of each feature level explicitly. Conclusions The pipeline provides a reproducible, extensible framework for deriving informative individual-level dynamic features from anatomy. The two-brain extension generates and ranks candidate inter-brain features, providing a principled way to identify between-brain measures for hypothesis-driven testing.

title: Resomapper: An integrated workflow for quantitative multiparametric MRI in preclinical studies.
abstract: Background Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (qMRI) provides insights into tissue microstructure and physiology, making it a tool in preclinical research. However, its processing often requires coding expertise. New method We present Resomapper, an open-source, cross-platform tool designed to simplify multiparametric MRI analysis. Resomapper integrates libraries into a user-friendly workflow that supports T 1 , T 2 , and T 2 * relaxometry mapping, magnetization transfer imaging, and diffusion tensor imaging. It incorporates preprocessing steps -including denoising, Gibbs artifact removal, and bias correction- and enables interactive and automated processing. Results Resomapper was applied to a multiparametric 7 T dataset of healthy mouse brain, generating T 1 , T 2 , T 2 *, magnetization transfer ratio and diffusion tensor maps. The values fell within the ranges reported in the literature and reproduced the differences between grey and white matter regions, illustrating its use in a preclinical study. Comparison with existing methods Resomapper distinguishes itself from qMRI tools not through novel algorithms, but through its integration of established, validated libraries into a single, streamlined pipeline for data conversion, preprocessing and parametric mapping. Maps showed excellent agreement with qMRLab for T 2 and were consistent with DSI Studio for mean and axial diffusivity, while systematic differences in radial diffusivity and fractional anisotropy were attributable to the tensor fitting methods. Its design prioritizes reproducibility and standardization, and its Python implementation makes the tool straightforward to install, inspect, and adapt, even for researchers without extensive coding backgrounds. Conclusions By improving accessibility, reproducibility, and standardization, Resomapper aims to facilitate broader adoption of qMRI in preclinical imaging despite current methodological challenges.

title: Osteoarthritis year in review 2026: Imaging.
abstract: Objective To narratively review the literature on osteoarthritis (OA) imaging published between March 2025 and March 2026 and to identify current trends and emerging directions in imaging-based OA research. Methods PubMed was searched for original English-language human in vivo studies published during the period. Trends by imaging modality and target-joint distributions were analyzed. For narrative synthesis, studies were selected subjectively by consensus among the authors based on methodological novelty, clinical or trial relevance, contribution to understanding OA pathophysiology or progression, and potential future impact. Results Of 1,910 publications identified, 1,035 specified a target joint. Approximately 70% investigated the knee, followed by the hip. Radiography and ultrasound yielded the most records, encompassing heterogeneous applications such as trial eligibility and image-guided procedures. Although publication counts for these modalities have gradually declined in recent years, those for MRI have remained stable. Semiquantitative MRI analysis linked worsening bone marrow lesions and Hoffa-synovitis to greater cartilage loss, and suggested differing associations between injection type and subsequent structural progression. Quantitative MRI studies linked cartilage T2 to BMI in a population-based cohort, while muscle radiomics predicted incident knee OA. Among emerging technique, magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) provided rapid cartilage T2 mapping, and [18F]NaF PET-MRI linked increased metabolic activity at enthesis to worse knee-related outcomes. For clinical-trial eligibility, MRI detected exclusionary abnormalities in 10% of otherwise DMOAD-eligible knees. AI-related publications gradually increased, with applications including prediction of future total knee replacement (TKR) and automated tissue segmentation. Conclusion Studies highlight the use of imaging for longitudinal assessment of structural progression, clinical-trial eligibility, and quantitative tissue characterization. MRI remains central to understanding disease mechanisms and progression, while emerging techniques such as MRF and [18F]NaF PET-MRI broaden quantitative and metabolic assessment. AI may support prediction of future TKR and automated cartilage morphometry.

title: Workflow-friendly free-breathing whole-chest cardiovascular MRI using inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state.
abstract: Background Free-breathing cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) may provide useful volumetric information. This study evaluated acquisition time and the feasibility of incorporating highly accelerated free-breathing inner-volume balanced T1 relaxation-enhanced steady-state (bT1RESS) imaging into a standard CMR protocol during the post-contrast interval before late gadolinium enhancement (LGE). Methods A prototype ECG-gated, navigator-gated inner-volume bT1RESS sequence was added to 1.5T CMR examinations in 45 patients; 30 were included in the paired comparison with breath-hold bT1RESS. Series-start timing was assessed in 14 of the 45 patients. Three readers assessed image quality. Aortic diameters were compared between bT1RESS protocols and, in an additional cohort of 15 subjects, with CEMRA. Agreement was assessed separately at five aortic levels using Bland-Altman analysis. Results Median inner-volume bT1RESS acquisition time was 1.82minutes (range, 0.78-3.72). In the series-start timing subset, median intervals from perfusion/CEMRA start to TI scout and first LGE series were 6.49minutes (n=13) and 8.46minutes (n=14), respectively. Reader preferences favored the inner-volume over breath-hold bT1RESS protocol. In the CEMRA comparison, mean differences (inner-volume bT1RESS minus CEMRA) ranged from 0.00 to 0.93mm; the lower and upper 95% limits of agreement ranged from -2.47 to -1.16mm and from 2.06 to 3.02mm, respectively. Conclusion Inner-volume bT1RESS provided rapid volumetric cardiovascular imaging within the evaluated post-contrast workflow. A primary benefit is the capability for 3D vessel measurement without a separate first-pass CEMRA acquisition. The technique may also help identify coronary artery origins, characterize morphological abnormalities in congenital heart disease and other cardiovascular disorders, and help to detect and characterize extracardiac lesions. Larger studies are needed to establish reproducibility and diagnostic performance.

In the series-start timing subset, median intervals from perfusion/CEMRA start to TI scout and first LGE series were 6.49minutes (n=13) and 8.46minutes (n=14), respectively. Conclusion

Inner-volume bT1RESS provided rapid volumetric cardiovascular imaging within the evaluated post-contrast workflow. A primary benefit is the capability for 3D vessel measurement without a separate first-pass CEMRA acquisition. The technique may also help identify coronary artery origins, characterize morphological abnormalities in congenital heart disease and other cardiovascular disorders, and help to detect and characterize extracardiac lesions. Larger studies are needed to establish reproducibility and diagnostic performance.

title: Dynamic Fractional Myocardial Blood Volume Mapping Using Ferumoxytol-enhanced CMR Multitasking with Subspace Dose Harmonization.
abstract: Background Fractional myocardial blood volume (fMBV) represents the vascular compartment within myocardial tissue and may reflect changes in microvascular status and health. Conventionally derived from multi-dose Modified Look-Locker Inversion (MOLLI) recovery T1 mapping with ferumoxytol, MOLLI-based fMBV requires repeated breath-holds, inter-dose image registration, and static end-diastolic estimates. CMR Multitasking enables free-breathing, non-electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated imaging and offers a subspace that captures shared motion and contrast dynamics. This subspace representation can be exploited to harmonize multi-dose acquisitions directly in parameter space, enabling motion-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping while reducing reliance on post-hoc image-space registration. Methods Thirteen healthy volunteers (11 females, 28.2±10.0 years) and twelve ischemic heart disease (IHD) patients (1 female, 67.2±7.1 years) underwent multi-dose ferumoxytol imaging at 3.0T using both breath-held ECG-triggered 5(3)3(3)3 MOLLI and free-running 2-dimensional Multitasking T1 mapping sequences. MOLLI-Multitasking agreement was assessed in healthy volunteers; patient data were used for exploratory dynamic fMBV analysis. Multitasking data were harmonized across respiratory- and cardiac-motion subspace dimensions for cross-dose alignment. Pixel-wise fMBV was estimated using a two-compartment water exchange model. fMBV agreement with MOLLI was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis. Dynamic fMBV changes were also evaluated from the Multitasking data. In IHD patients, fMBV kinetic metrics (upslope and diastolic-to-systolic distribution) for cycle-dependent variation in dynamic fMBV were computed to assess systolic compression and diastolic recoil. Cardiac positron emission tomography (PET) derived perfusion and CMR-derived strain and late gadolinium enhancement served as references. Results In healthy volunteers, Multitasking produced motion-resolved fMBV maps with strong MOLLI agreement (bias -0.11%, p=0.84). Subspace harmonization reduced cross-dose variability and aligned cardiac phases. Healthy subjects showed significant diastolic-to-systolic variation (10.55±2.12% vs. 7.73±2.76%, p=0.0004). In IHD patients, ischemic segments exhibited elevated diastolic fMBV with significant systolic compression (16.36±3.44% vs. 10.01±2.24%, p=0.013), remote myocardium showed similar phasic variation (11.16±0.68% vs. 7.98±0.57%, p<0.0001). At the same time, scar demonstrated reduced fMBV with attenuated modulation (7.74±1.95% vs. 5.59±1.97%, p=0.099). Abnormal dynamic fMBV regions corresponded to PET defects and impaired circumferential strain. Conclusion Ferumoxytol-enhanced Multitasking with subspace harmonization enables free-breathing, cardiac-resolved dynamic fMBV mapping, overcoming practical limitations of MOLLI-derived fMBV. This approach enables non-invasive assessment of dynamic myocardial blood volume across the cardiac cycle, with potential utility for characterizing microvascular function in ischemic heart disease.

title: Precision localization of spinal cord lesions during surgery: Current technologies and future directions for targeted therapies.
abstract: Background Accurate intraoperative localization is essential for safe spinal cord surgery. Although numerous imaging, navigation, and neurophysiological technologies are available, their contributions are generally discussed individually rather than according to the information they provide for surgical decision-making. Emerging targeted intramedullary therapies introduce additional requirements for precise therapeutic delivery. Objective To critically review established and emerging intraoperative guidance technologies in spinal cord surgery and propose an information-centered framework supporting indication-specific surgical decision-making and precision therapeutic targeting. Methods A narrative review of the literature was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, supplemented by relevant references from selected publications. Technologies were evaluated according to their clinical applications, supporting evidence, limitations, and contribution to intraoperative guidance. Results Five complementary information domains were identified: anatomical localization, morphological characterization, functional localization, tissue characterization, and precision therapeutic targeting. Established techniques, particularly intraoperative ultrasound and neurophysiological monitoring, provide clinically relevant guidance in selected spinal cord procedures. Fluorescence imaging offers additional vascular or tumor-associated information, whereas advanced optical imaging, multimodal fusion, artificial intelligence, and robotic assistance remain insufficiently validated for routine intramedullary applications. The proposed framework emphasizes that these domains are neither mandatory nor sequential and that additional technological complexity does not necessarily translate into improved clinical outcomes. Emerging targeted therapies further highlight the distinction between instrument positioning accuracy, therapeutic deposition, and effective biological exposure. Conclusions An information-centered approach may help guide the selection and integration of intraoperative technologies according to surgical objectives and clinical evidence. Future developments should prioritize validated, indication-specific strategies demonstrating improvements in procedural safety, targeting accuracy, and patient-relevant outcomes.

title: Percutaneous screw distraction versus open fusion surgery for anatomic restoration after burst fracture.
abstract: Background Open posterior transpedicular screw fixation for thoracolumbar burst fractures involves substantial muscle dissection, resulting in iatrogenic trauma, prolonged hospital stays, and extended recovery times, but minimally invasive techniques like percutaneous pedicle screw fixation cannot be used in all fracture patterns or indications. We compared perioperative and radiographic outcomes of a fixed-angle percutaneous instrumentation technique versus conventional open fixation in patients managed without direct decompression. Methods In this retrospective cohort study at our Level I trauma center, patients who underwent either open or percutaneous instrumentation without laminectomy in 2018-2024 were identified. Patients with AO Spine fracture classifications of A2, A3, and A4 were present in the cohort. Student's t-test and Pearson's Chi-square statistical tests were used to compare the perioperative and radiographic outcomes of patients who underwent fixed-angle percutaneous instrumentation with those who underwent conventional open fixation without direct decompression. Results Among 63 included patients, 24 underwent percutaneous surgery and 39 had open procedures. Selection varied by on-call surgeon, not fracture characteristics. AO Spine fracture classifications (A2, A3, A4) were similarly distributed between groups (p = 0.25). Baseline characteristics were similar between groups. The percutaneous group experienced significantly less intraoperative blood loss (p < 0.001), showed greater improvement in canal cross-sectional area from preoperative to postoperative (p = 0.01), and had greater improvement in vertebral body index scores from postdistraction to last follow-up (p = 0.02). The groups were statistically similar in all other radiographic outcomes. Elective instrumentation removal was more frequent in patients in the percutaneous cohort (p = 0.001). Conclusions Percutaneous instrumentation for thoracolumbar burst fractures not involving decompression achieved radiographic outcomes comparable with open techniques in this study. The percutaneous technique demonstrated favorable radiographic outcomes, with greater indirect canal decompression intraoperatively and better vertebral body index scores at last follow-up. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective comparison.

title: Callosal atrophy does not establish physiological disconnection in imaging models of cognitive risk in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Automated magnetic resonance imaging can quantify callosal atrophy and estimate structural disconnection in multiple sclerosis, but neither measurement establishes physiological conduction failure. In an early relapsing-remitting cohort, Wahl and colleagues found a relationship between motor-callosal microstructure and interhemispheric inhibition in controls that was not detectable in patients. This finding illustrates why a structural feature cannot automatically inherit a functional interpretation. Earlier structure-function studies provide a foundation for contemporary pipelines when the measurements, pathways, and populations are comparable. This opinion paper organizes validation into five evidence domains with separate biological and prognostic branches: technical validity, biological validity, physiological validity, prognostic performance, and clinical utility. Physiological claims require functional evidence matched to anatomy and task, with reliability and competing circuit explanations assessed. A purely prognostic feature instead requires credible predictive evaluation, including external validation and calibration; it may be useful as a proxy for global disease burden. Clinical utility concerns the consequences of a specified decision and is distinct from predictive performance and implementation feasibility. Reports should preserve the qualifier in estimated structural disconnection and reserve physiological interpretations for measurements supported by corresponding functional evidence.

title: Hydraulic pressure sinus lift versus piezoelectric lift via lateral approach: A randomized controlled clinical trial.
abstract: Introduction To assess the effectiveness of hydraulic pressure sinus lift via lateral wall approach versus piezoelectric surgery in patients with deficient posterior maxilla. Materials and methods This study involved a randomized clinical trial of 20 participants with less than 6 mm of bone height in the posterior maxilla in need of Maxillary Sinus Floor Augmentation using the lateral window approach. Patients were randomly assigned to two groups; the HPLT Group included 10 patients who underwent hydraulic pressure for osteotomy preparation for the lateral sinus lifting technique, while the PSLT Group included 10 patients managed using piezoelectric surgery. Clinical and radiographic assessment of bone augmentation, as well as intraoperative biological complications and postoperative complications, were recorded. Results Both groups showed insignificant differences in the recorded procedural duration, intraoperative complications, and reported postoperative pain. The HPLT group reported a statistically significant increase in bone height, with a mean height gain of 6.81 ± 1.85. The PSLT group reported a mean height gain of 5.51 ± 0.90. The difference between the compared groups regarding the final gain in bone height was statistically insignificant (P = 0.061). Discussion Both hydraulic pressure-assisted and piezoelectric lateral sinus floor elevation resulted in increased radiographic bone height at six months, without a statistically significant difference between groups. Although these findings support the feasibility of hydraulic pressure-assisted sinus augmentation, the limited sample size prevents definitive conclusions regarding its comparative effectiveness and safety.

title: Ovary-Sparing Surgery for Coexisting Mature Cystic Teratoma and Ovarian Hemangioma in a 7-Year-Old Girl: A Case Report.
abstract: Study objective To describe ovary-sparing management of coexisting mature cystic teratoma and ovarian hemangioma in a child. Methods A 7-year-old girl with periumbilical pain and early pubertal signs underwent endocrine, radiologic, and surgical evaluation of a complex pelvic mass. Results Endocrine assessment, including age-concordant bone age, supported premature pubarche without evidence of central precocious puberty. An isolated inhibin B elevation normalized 12 days later before surgery and remained normal postoperatively; other tumor markers and hormones were normal. Serial imaging variably suggested uterine or ovarian origin. Left ovarian lesions were completely excised through a Pfannenstiel approach while preserving follicle-containing ovarian tissue. Final pathology demonstrated a 5.5-cm hemangioma adjacent to a 2.5-cm mature teratoma. Recovery was uneventful, with no recurrence or pubertal progression during 2 years of 6-monthly follow-up. Conclusion Decisions regarding ovary-sparing surgery should integrate preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging findings with intraoperative assessment; definitive histopathology establishes the final diagnosis.

title: Building plant 3D digital twins via AI-powered cell atlases: technological advances, applications, and future perspectives.
abstract: Plant organ function is governed by the precise spatial arrangement and coordinated interactions of constituent cells. Immobilized by rigid cell walls, plant cells develop in place, and their positions and adjacency relationships form a three-dimensional (3D) topological network that underpins tissue architecture and organ morphogenesis. Conventional two-dimensional (2D) sectioning, however, discretizes this continuous topology into isolated planes, severing native cell adjacency and obscuring global organ architecture, whereas volumetric imaging preserves cellular coordinates, geometry and connectivity in situ. Recent advances in multimodal cross-scale imaging have enabled high-resolution 3D visualization spanning from subcellular structures to intact organs. In parallel, deep-learning-based segmentation has increasingly resolved bottlenecks in densely packed plant tissues, facilitating the construction of computable digital cell atlases. In this review, we synthesize progress in the intelligent 3D interpretation of plant multicellular systems, surveying the technical capabilities of multimodal imaging regarding penetration depth, spatial resolution, and four-dimensional (4D) dynamic tracking, alongside deep-learning strategies to overcome structural constraints imposed by rigid cell walls. Furthermore, diverse applications of digital cell atlases in morphological phenotyping, mechanical inference, topological network analysis, and spatial multi-omics integration are examined, underscoring their role as the foundational data substrate for plant digital twins. We further distinguish digital cell atlases from predictive digital twins and highlight plant-specific challenges, including optical barriers of plant tissues, cross-lineage model transfer and deployment in breeding. We conclude by discussing the transition from static reconstructions toward predictive digital twins of plant tissues and organs, providing a methodological framework to elucidate plant organ morphogenesis.

title: Subfield-specific hippocampal enlargement in high-functioning autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: Although previous studies have reported abnormal hippocampal volumes in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), the specific alterations in hippocampal subfields and their relationships with clinical symptoms in high-functioning ASD (HF-ASD) remain unclear. In this study, we analyzed T1-weighted structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I (ABIDE-I), including 182 children and adolescents with HF-ASD and 213 age- and sex-matched typically developing controls (TDC). Using a linear mixed-effects model, we compared hippocampal volumes between groups, and examined associations between volumes and clinical measurements. Compared to TDC, the children and adolescents with HF-ASD exhibited significantly increased volumes in the right entire hippocampus, presubiculum, subiculum, and granule cell layer of the dentate gyrus (GC-DG). No significant volumetric differences were observed within the child or adolescent subgroups, nor between these age groups. Notably, presubiculum volume showed a positive correlation with verbal scores and a negative correlation with social scores in the HF-ASD group. These findings indicate subfield-specific hippocampal overgrowth in children and adolescents with HF-ASD and presubiculum volume alteration may be a potential neuroanatomical correlate underlying verbal and social dysfunctions.

title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
abstract: Background Prosthetic joint infection (PJI) following shoulder arthroplasty is difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are often nonspecific, conventional diagnostic tests have variable sensitivity, and Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) may cause indolent infection with limited systemic inflammatory response. Diagnostic criteria have also largely been adapted from hip and knee arthroplasty with limited shoulder-specific validation. This International Consensus Meeting (ICM) reviewed the available evidence and developed consensus recommendations for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI. Methods The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts experienced in shoulder arthroplasty and PJI. Thirty-two diagnostic questions underwent question-specific literature review, presentation to the consensus group, discussion, and voting. A modified Delphi process was used to establish consensus. Delegates voted to agree, disagree, or abstain. Consensus was categorized by percentage agreement, while strength of recommendation was assessed separately based on evidence quality, consistency, and directness. Results Consensus was achieved for 31 analyzed questions, with agreement ranging from 72% to 100%; 29 resulted in recommendations for clinical practice and 2 were identified as requiring further research. Question 47, which addressed the definition of PJI, was reported separately. Humeral component loosening, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were supported as components of the diagnostic criteria, whereas cloudy fluid, postoperative stiffness, serum WBC count, and D-dimer were not supported as independent criteria. Arthroscopic tissue biopsy, frozen section, and selective ultrasound-guided aspiration or synovial biopsy were supported as adjuncts to diagnosis. Five intraoperative tissue specimens, prolonged aerobic and anaerobic culture incubation, and routine perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis were supported. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and synovial neutrophil testing were supported as adjuncts; alpha-defensin was considered potentially useful but insufficiently validated for formal inclusion; and leukocyte esterase inclusion was not recommended. Routine use of bone scintigraphy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), or positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) was not supported. Evidence remained insufficient to determine the clinical significance of polymicrobial molecular results or routine negative control samples. Conclusion The 2025 ICM provides a consensus framework for the diagnosis of shoulder PJI, identifying several measures that can be incorporated into current clinical practice. However, substantial uncertainty remains because most recommendations are supported by limited evidence and several diagnostic tests lack sufficient sensitivity. Prospective, shoulder-specific studies are needed to define diagnostic thresholds and determine the role of emerging molecular, biomarker, and imaging modalities.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Resisted Anterior Drawer (RAD) Test for Lateral Elbow Instability in Lateral Epicondylitis.
abstract: Background Lateral epicondylitis (LE) is increasingly recognized as a multifactorial condition in which subtle lateral elbow instability may contribute to persistent pain. However, reliable clinical tests to detect such instability are lacking. Purpose To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the resisted anterior drawer (RAD) test for detecting lateral elbow instability in patients with LE. Methods Consecutive adult patients diagnosed with LE underwent standardized clinical examination followed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The RAD test was considered positive when pain during resisted wrist extension, with the elbow in extension, decreased by at least 1 point on a visual analogue scale (VAS) with anteromedial stabilization of the radial head. MRI-defined instability was defined as the presence of lateral collateral ligament (LCL) injury, posterior sagging, or ulnohumeral joint-line opening of grade ≥1. Diagnostic indices were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and likelihood ratios, and the continuous reduction in pain was evaluated with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results A total of 500 elbows were analyzed (mean age: 51 years). MRI evidence of instability was present in 57.4% of elbows. The RAD test demonstrated a sensitivity of 95.8% (95% CI 92.8-97.6%), specificity of 82.2% (95% CI 76.5-86.7%), and overall accuracy of 90.0% (95% CI 87.1-92.3%), with positive and negative likelihood ratios of 5.4 and 0.05. The area under the ROC curve for the reduction in pain was 0.92 (95% CI 0.90-0.95). The magnitude of pain reduction during the RAD maneuver correlated with the severity of MRI-defined instability (Spearman ρ = -0.71). Increasing MRI severity was associated with a higher number of corticosteroid infiltrations, whereas symptom duration showed only a weak association with structural instability. Conclusion In this Level III diagnostic study, the RAD test showed high sensitivity and good specificity for MRI-defined lateral elbow instability in patients with LE, and the magnitude of pain reduction was correlated with MRI-defined severity. These findings suggest that the RAD test may be a useful screening maneuver for instability-related pain in patients with LE. A prospective, blinded cohort study with an independent reference standard is required to confirm its clinical utility. Level of evidence Level III, Diagnostic Study.

title: Functional outcomes over 24 months after arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tendon tears in a multicentre study.
abstract: Background Isolated subscapularis tears are rare, and it is currently unclear how the tear size relates to the postoperative outcomes after arthroscopic repair. This study aimed to evaluate clinical- and patient-reported outcomes, as well as adverse events of arthroscopically treated isolated subscapularis tears based on the tear extent over 24 months. Methods Across 19 orthopaedic centres, 69 patients undergoing primary arthroscopic repair for isolated subscapularis tears were prospectively recruited between June 2020 and November 2021. Medical imaging examinations were conducted at baseline and at 12 months. Clinical- and patient-reported outcomes were obtained at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months. Adverse events within 24 months were documented. Patients were grouped into partial tears (n = 14), full-thickness tears of the superior half (n = 35) or complete full-thickness tears (n = 20) of the subscapularis. All outcomes were compared using generalised linear mixed models adjusted for baseline values, age, sex, American Society of Anaesthesiologists classification, tear aetiology, and steroid infiltrations. Results Improvements in all outcome scores were observed after surgery. No group differences were observed in the ranges of motion in flexion, abduction and external rotation (P≥0.634). The partial tear group had a higher pain level than both full-thickness groups at 12 months (P≤0.005). Abduction strength, Constant Score, Oxford Shoulder Score, Subjective Shoulder Value and EQ-5D-5L showed positive changes within 12- or 24-month follow-ups, with no group differences (P≥0.089). The risk of at least a symptomatic adverse event of any severity level affecting the operated shoulder and arm was highest for patients with partial tears (50%) and lowest for patients with complete full-thickness tears (25%). The most frequent occurrences were persistent or worsening pain, stiffness, and recurrent defects. Overall, 62% of patients with partial tears, 97% of patients with superior full-thickness tears and 77% of patients with complete full-thickness tears were satisfied at 24 months. Conclusion Arthroscopic repair of isolated subscapularis tears leads to significant and sustained improvements in clinical and patient-reported outcomes over 24 months, regardless of tear extent. However, patients with partial tears demonstrated greater residual pain and fewer patients reported satisfaction compared with those with full-thickness tears. These findings may reflect differences in patient characteristics and surgical treatment choices. Further studies are needed to determine the suitability and efficacy of surgical treatments for isolated subscapularis partial tears. Level of evidence Level III, Retrospective Cohort Comparison, Prognosis Study.

title: Surgical Treatment of Trans-ulnar Basal Coronoid Fracture-Dislocations: Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes in 34 Patients at a Mean 4-Year Follow-up.
abstract: Background Trans-ulnar basal coronoid (TUBC) fracture-dislocations represent a highly unstable pattern of elbow injury, characterized by a fracture through the base of the coronoid process that separates it from both the olecranon and the ulnar metaphysis. In TUBC fracture-dislocations, anatomic reduction and stable fixation of the coronoid are critical for restoring elbow function. The purpose of the present study was to evaluate the clinical and radiographic outcomes of patients surgically treated for TUBC fracture-dislocations. We analyzed fracture morphology, associated lesions, surgical approaches, coronoid fixation techniques, complications, and potential prognostic factors associated with inferior clinical outcomes. Materials and methods A retrospective review was performed of all patients surgically treated for TUBC fracture-dislocations at a single institution between 2012 and 2025 with a minimum clinical and radiographic follow-up of 12 months. Preoperative computed tomography scans were assessed to characterize fracture morphology and associated lesions. Clinical evaluation included elbow range of motion, Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), Broberg and Morrey (B&M) score, QuickDASH, and Single Assessment Numeric Evaluation (SANE). Radiographs were reviewed to assess fracture healing and radiographic complications. Results Thirty-four patients were included, with a mean age of 51.8 years. Mean clinical and radiographic follow-up were 48 and 43.1 months, respectively. A radial head fracture was present in 28 patients. At final follow-up, mean elbow flexion-extension arc was 117.2°. Mean forearm rotation arc was 154.2°. Mean MEPS and B&M scores were 92.3 and 90.5 points, respectively, whereas mean QuickDASH and SANE scores were 14.8 and 85.6 points, respectively. Coronoid comminution (≥ 3 fragments) was associated with higher odds of a non-excellent MEPS (<90 points). Union of the proximal ulna was achieved in all cases; 2 cases of asymptomatic coronoid tip nonunion, and 2 cases of asymptomatic coronoid plate breakage were observed. Overall, 21 complications in 15 patients (44.1%) were recorded; 5 revision surgeries in 4 patients (11.8%) were performed. Conclusions TUBC fracture-dislocations are complex injuries characterized by substantial variability in fracture morphology, in which accurate reduction and stable fixation of the coronoid are considered essential for achieving favorable outcomes. Most patients in the present series achieved satisfactory functional outcomes, with good or excellent MEPS results in more than 90% of cases. However, the overall complication rate remained substantial (44.1%) with a reoperation rate of 11.8%. A key finding of this study was that coronoid comminution was associated with poorer functional outcomes and higher odds of non-excellent MEPS results.

title: CT-Based Morphology and Outcomes After ORIF of Humeral Head Articular Fractures.
abstract: Background Articular fractures of the humeral head encompass a spectrum of injuries. CT-based assessment of the extent of articular injury may influence reduction, functional outcomes, and avascular necrosis (AVN), but its association with outcomes after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) remains incompletely understood. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 109 patients with humeral head articular fractures treated between 2010 and 2023 and classified fractures into five types using preoperative CT. Outcomes were analysed in 78 patients undergoing ORIF (mean age, 43 years; range, 20-68; SD, 11). Functional scores, reduction quality, and AVN incidence were compared across fracture types; complications and reoperations were recorded. Age and sex adjusted Constant scores (CS) and QuickDASH scores were assessed at a mean follow-up of 62 months (range, 24-122; SD, 18) after index ORIF. Exploratory multivariable analyses evaluated associations between fracture type and functional outcomes after adjustment for selected patient and injury characteristics. Reduction quality was graded as anatomical, acceptable, or poor using predefined radiographic criteria. Post-arthroplasty functional outcomes were analysed separately. Results Union was achieved in 72 of 78 patients (92%). Mean CS was 69 (range, 28-100; SD, 18) and mean QuickDASH was 29 (range, 2.3-61.4; SD, 14). Functional outcomes differed among fracture types (CS and QuickDASH, both p < 0.001), with poorer function in types 3-5. These associations persisted after adjustment for tuberosity involvement and articular fragment dislocation, with additional adjustment for age and sex for the QuickDASH model (p < 0.001 for both CS and QuickDASH). Anatomical reduction was more frequent in types 1 and 2 than types 3- 5 (p = 0.018). AVN developed in 14 patients (18%), exclusively in types 3-5 (p = 0.015). 12 (15%) patients underwent conversion arthroplasty after failed ORIF. At a mean of 21 months after salvage arthroplasty, significant improvements were observed in CS (mean increase, 23.7 points, p < 0.001) and QuickDASH scores (mean decrease, 21.4 points, p < 0.001) CONCLUSIONS: Most humeral head articular fractures healed after ORIF with acceptable clinical outcomes. Fractures with complete articular separation, comminution, and associated articular impaction, were associated with less frequent anatomical reduction, more AVN, and poorer shoulder and upper limb function. CT-based characterization may facilitate assessment of the extent of articular injury and its association with outcomes, although independent validation is required. title: Subscapularis Healing and the Associated Impact on Outcomes Following Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background The role of subscapularis repair following reverse shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) remains controversial, particularly regarding restoration of internal rotation and postoperative function. While prior studies have compared repair versus non-repair, few have evaluated postoperative tendon integrity using ultrasound. Without direct assessment of tendon healing, functional differences cannot be reliably attributed to repair status. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the relationship between subscapularis healing and clinical outcomes following rTSA. Methods A retrospective review of prospectively collected data was performed of patients undergoing primary lateralized rTSA from 2022-2025 by a single surgeon. Patients underwent subscapularis repair with optional augmentation. Subscapularis repair was classified as healed or non-healed based on ultrasound evaluation at minimum 10-weeks. Patients with at least 1-year follow-up and postoperative ultrasound evaluation of the subscapularis were included. Patients with preoperative fractures or full-thickness subscapularis tears were excluded. Outcomes included VAS pain score, ASES score, SST score, range of motion, strength testing, and complication rates. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between augmentation and healing, adjusting for ultrasound timing and sex. Multivariable linear regression assessed the association between healing and postoperative ROM at 12 and 24 months, adjusting for preoperative motion and posterosuperior rotator cuff integrity. Significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Of 235 patients who underwent subscapularis repair, 126 shoulders (118 patients) met inclusion criteria. Healing was observed in 100 patients (79.4%). Healed repairs were significantly associated with augmentation (84.9% vs. 67.5%, p = .025), however, this association was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for ultrasound timing and sex (p = .113). Healed tendons demonstrated lower VAS pain (0 vs 1, p = 0.014) and ASES scores at 24 months (92 vs. 85, p = .022), though these differences are below the MCID. Internal rotation was improved at 12 months (6 vs. 4, p = 0.017). Healing was not independently associated with forward elevation, abduction, external rotation, or internal rotation at 12 or 24 months after multivariable adjustment. Complications occurred in 7.0% of patients with healed repairs and none with non-healed repairs (p = .343). Conclusion Sonographically intact subscapularis repairs following lateralized rTSA were associated with greater internal rotation at 1-year, however it was not independently associated with postoperative ROM after adjustment. This study represents one of the largest cohorts of sonographically evaluated subscapularis repairs following RTSA. Further investigation of biologic augmentation strategies may help improve subscapularis repair outcomes in rTSA. Level of evidence Level III; Retrospective Cohort Comparison; Prognosis Study.

title: Association of Respiratory-Related Sarcopenia Classification With Postoperative Complications and Overall Survival in Older Patients With Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Introduction Respiratory function and muscle measures have previously been studied together. We evaluated a classification combining peak expiratory flow and a computed tomography-derived pectoralis muscle index in older patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Methods This retrospective cohort included 742 patients aged ≥65 y undergoing minimally invasive McKeown esophagectomy during 2020-2021. Pectoralis muscle index was the bilateral pectoralis major area at T4 divided by height squared, a surrogate of chest-wall muscle reserve. Two isolated-abnormality phenotypes were combined exploratorily into mild, alongside normal and severe categories. Logistic and Cox regression evaluated associations. Survival discrimination was assessed in the development cohort; stratified Cox sensitivity analyses addressed nonproportional hazards. Results Normal, mild, and severe comprised 340, 310, and 92 patients. Adjusted pneumonia odds ratios versus normal were 1.548 (95% confidence interval, 1.039-2.306) for mild and 2.973 (1.746-5.064) for severe. The leakage model retained no other covariates. In the T/N-stratified survival model, hazard ratios were 2.445 (1.948-3.067) and 3.585 (2.618-4.908), respectively. Adding the classification increased the apparent C-index from 0.837 to 0.861. Pneumonia areas under the curve were 0.616 for the four-group framework and 0.613 for the simplified classification. Conclusions The classification was associated with postoperative outcomes and overall survival. Its simpler grouping had observed discrimination close to the four-group framework. However, its clinical utility in preoperative optimization still requires further validation in prospective studies.

title: Low-dose CT Screening and Smoking Cessation: Separate and Joint Associations with Mortality among Ever-Smokers Eligible for Lung Cancer Screening.
abstract: Background Smoking cessation intervention is increasingly recognized as a core component of high-quality lung cancer screening (LCS). However, real-world evidence that compares the health effects of low-dose CT (LDCT) screening, smoking cessation, and their combination among screening-eligible current smokers remains limited. Methods We conducted a post-hoc analysis of data of the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), defining recent quitting as smoking cessation within 2 years before enrolment as a proxy for cessation occurring close to screening initiation. Cox proportional hazards models were used to quantify associations of screening allocation and smoking cessation with LC-specific and all-cause mortality. Results Among 31,560 continuous smokers and recent quitters included in the analysis, 7,197 (22.8%) died from any cause during a median follow-up of 12.3 years. Of 30,915 participants included in cause-specific analyses, 1,783 (5.8%) died from LC. Among current smokers eligible for LCS, LDCT was associated with 12% lower LC mortality than chest radiography (CXR) (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.97), but no significant reduction of all-cause mortality (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.03). In the CXR arm, recent quitting was associated with substantially lower LC and all-cause mortality than continued smoking (HRs, 0.62 and 0.68; 95% CIs, 0.51-0.76 and 0.62-0.75, respectively), with similar reductions observed among recent quitters in the LDCT arm. Conclusions For screening-eligible current smokers, recent quitting was associated with substantially larger reductions in LC and all-cause mortality than those associated with LDCT screening. These findings reinforce the importance of integrating effective smoking cessation interventions into LCS programs.

title: Acoustic Correlates of Endoscopically Identified Vocal Fold Lesions in a Large Clinical Cohort: Perceptual Associations and Screening Performance.
abstract: Benign vocal fold lesions are among the most common causes of dysphonia, yet large cohort studies integrating endoscopic, perceptual, and acoustic domains remain scarce. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of vocal fold lesions in a large clinical cohort and to determine acoustic characteristics linked to endoscopically detected vocal fold lesions and able to differentiate them from structurally normal vocal folds, corroborated by perceptual severity ratings. Methods In this cross-sectional cohort study, 782 patients with dysphonia underwent videolaryngostroboscopy, standardized acoustic recording, and auditory-perceptual evaluation using the Consensus Auditory-Perceptual Evaluation of Voice (CAPE-V) and GRBAS scales. Acoustic parameters (jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio [HNR], and smoothed cepstral peak prominence [CPPS]) were compared across lesion categories and entered into multivariable logistic regression models. Results Vocal fold polyps were the most prevalent lesion (32.1%), followed by nodules (24.0%), Reinke's edema (16.0%), cysts (13.9%), and granuloma (7.9%). All acoustic parameters differed significantly across categories (P < .001), with polyps showing the greatest deviation from normal values. CPPS was the strongest independent predictor of lesion presence (adjusted OR 1.62 per 1-dB decrease, P < .001) and correlated most strongly with CAPE-V overall severity (r = -.71, P < .001). The combined acoustic model discriminated lesion from non-lesion voices with excellent accuracy (AUC = 0.91). Conclusions Acoustic changes, such as decreased CPPS and HNR and increased jitter and shimmer, were related to vocal fold lesions identified by endoscopy. CPPS had the greatest separation between patients with a lesion, identified endoscopically, and structurally normal patients. These acoustic measures should be viewed as a screening/triage marker of vocal fold abnormality and not as a marker of benignity or lesion-specific etiology, however, because the study excluded malignant, neurological, and other major voice pathologies. Acoustic assessment is thus a useful non-invasive complement to laryngeal endoscopic assessment, but should not replace it.

title: MONKEY Challenge: Machine-learning for Optimal detection of iNflammatory cells in KidnEY transplant biopsies.
abstract: Purpose Accurate quantification of inflammatory cells in Periodic Acid-Schiff (PAS)-stained kidney transplant biopsies is essential for Banff classification but remains subjective and labor-intensive. To address this, the MONKEY challenge benchmarked deep learning (DL) methods for automated detection of mononuclear leukocytes and their subtypes. Materials and methods A multicenter dataset of 118 biopsies with co-registered PAS and immunohistochemically restained slides, comprising over 131,000 annotated cells, was used. The algorithms were evaluated on hold-out validation and test set using Free-response Receiver Operating Characteristic (FROC) analysis, alongside precision, recall, and F1-scores. Results Across diverse architectures, performance converged, with the top models achieving F1-scores up to 0.75 for overall detection. Lymphocyte detection performed well (F1 up to 0.78), whereas monocyte detection remained more challenging (F1 up to 0.47). To explore the potential clinical applicability of automated inflammatory cell detection, the winning model was integrated with renal tissue segmentation models, enabling compartment-specific evaluation and quantitative assessment of Banff-related lesions. In an independent multicenter cohort of 180 kidney transplant biopsies, DL-derived quantitative measurements demonstrated strong correlations with consensus pathologist scoring for several inflammation-related Banff lesions, particularly total inflammation and interstitial inflammation. Conclusions This study establishes the first multicenter, PAS-based, IHC-validated benchmark for inflammatory cell detection and provides a clinically grounded resource to support the development of robust, generalizable AI systems for transplant pathology. Beyond benchmark performance, our extended tissue-specific analyses demonstrate that inflammatory cell detection on routine PAS slides can be anatomically contextualized and translated into quantitative measurements that align with conventional Banff lesion assessment, providing a foundation for future AI-assisted evaluation of kidney transplant biopsies.

title: Prognostic Significance of AI-Quantified Central Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes in Bladder Cancer.
abstract: Purpose Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are associated with clinical outcomes in bladder cancer; however, conventional assessment methods are limited by subjective scoring and interobserver variability. We aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of TILs at both the tumor center and invasive front using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based quantification approach across two independent bladder cancer cohorts. Materials and methods We analyzed 84 patients with urothelial carcinoma who underwent TURB at a single institution. Pathologists selected tumor center and invasive front regions, and an AI pipeline combining tissue segmentation and lymphocyte detection measured the TIL ratio in each region. As an independent cohort, we analyzed The Cancer Genome Atlas bladder urothelial carcinoma (TCGA-BLCA) dataset, in which the two regions were identified by a whole-slide model with a pathologist-in-the-loop system. Each cohort was dichotomized at its respective median. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, the log-rank test, and Cox regression. Results In the TURB cohort (75 patients with measurable central TILs, 44 recurrences), a high central TIL ratio was associated with longer RFS (log-rank p=0.019; hazard ratio [HR] 0.495, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.271-0.902, p=0.022). This association remained significant in models adjusted for pathological T category and age. In the TCGA-BLCA cohort, our AI model detected tumor center and invasive front areas with a pathologist-in-the-loop system, and a high central (tumor center) TIL density was associated with longer RFS in 38 patients (p=0.022) and with longer OS in 77 patients (p=0.037). TIL density at the invasive front was not associated with outcomes in either cohort. Conclusions AI-based quantification of TILs at the tumor center was associated with favorable survival outcomes across two independent bladder cancer cohorts, whereas measurements at the invasive front showed no significant prognostic association. These findings support the potential prognostic relevance of spatially resolved TIL assessment in bladder cancer and warrant further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Spatial Profiling Reveals Gland-Resolved Epithelial and Immune Features Associated With Progression in Localized Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Purpose Gleason grading remains central to localized prostate cancer diagnosis but incompletely captures the biological heterogeneity associated with disease progression. We integrated spatial proteomics, gland-resolved histopathology, and an AI-assisted functional tissue unit (FTU) annotation workflow to characterize epithelial and immune heterogeneity across Gleason patterns and longitudinal changes during active surveillance. Materials and methods Cyclic immunofluorescence (cycIF) imaging with antibody panels of up to 40 markers was performed on radical prostatectomy and longitudinal active surveillance specimens. Using MiroSCOPE, a human-in-the-loop AI-assisted pathology workflow, we analyzed more than 35,000 pathologist-annotated FTUs. Multiplex marker correlations and immune cell densities were analyzed within spatially defined regions surrounding individually annotated glands. Results Gland-resolved spatial profiling revealed molecular heterogeneity across Gleason patterns, including increased AR, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, and Ki67 expression in non-cribriform Gleason pattern 4 glands from high-grade compared with low-grade tumors. Spatial analysis of individual glandular microenvironments revealed reduced macrophage and T-cell densities surrounding tumoral glands, whereas atrophic glands exhibited increased lymphoid and macrophage infiltration compared with normal glands. Longitudinal active surveillance analyses revealed progression-associated changes in periglandular immune populations, with increasing T-cell densities in non-progressors and declining T-cell and macrophage densities in progressors. Conclusions Gland-resolved spatial profiling reveals epithelial molecular heterogeneity within and across Gleason patterns and demonstrates that local immune organization varies according to glandular histopathology. Longitudinal reductions in periglandular T-cell and macrophage populations accompany histopathological progression, identifying spatial immune features that warrant further investigation as potential biomarkers of progression risk during active surveillance.

title: Performance of artificial intelligence versus clinician left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI for mortality prediction: a retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study.
abstract: Background Ejection fraction, a key measure of cardiac function, is used in health care for clinical decision making and risk stratification. We hypothesised that a deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) segmentation of ejection fraction obtained from cardiac MRI (CMR) outperforms expert clinician segmentation for the prediction of all-cause mortality. Methods In this retrospective, multicentre, prognostic study, we studied a cohort of 27 382 consecutive patients who underwent cardiac MRI (CMR) in the UK and the USA. Patients were referred for CMR from nine hospitals to Barts Heart Centre (BHC), London. Patients were identified from the reporting archive at BHC as having undergone a CMR between Oct 1, 2014 and Dec 31, 2019. A further cohort of patients was also identified from University of Pittsburgh Medical Centre (UPMC), Pittsburgh, PA, USA, as having undergone a CMR between June 1, 2010 and March 31, 2016. Mortality data were obtained from national and local databases. AI segmentation was done on all CMR studies, and Cox proportional hazards models were fitted to compare the prognostic value of AI-measured versus clinician-measured left-ventricular volume metrics. Model fit was compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), discrimination using C indices and the incremental value of AI over clinician segmentation using likelihood-ratio tests of nested models. Findings 27 382 patients received a baseline CMR (26 106 patients from BHC and 1276 from UPMC). The median follow-up was 5·6 years (IQR 4·4-6·9), during which 3458 (13%) of 27 382 patients died. AI ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 57 936 vs 58 097, ΔAIC 161 favouring AI) and marginally better discrimination (C index 0·669 vs 0·637; ΔC 0·033 [95% CI 0·026-0·041]). AI ejection fraction significantly improved model fit when added to clinician ejection fraction (χ 2 =168, p<0·0001), with only slight improvement when clinician ejection fraction was added to AI (χ 2 =7·5, p=0·023). After adjustment for age and sex, AI-derived ejection fraction showed better model fit (AIC 55 684 vs 55 742; ΔAIC 59) and had marginally better discrimination (C index of 0·781 vs 0·777; ΔC=0·004 [95% CI 0·002-0·006]). Interpretation AI-derived ejection fraction shows marginally superior prediction for mortality than clinician-derived ejection fraction in patients who had CMR. Findings support the potential utility of AI for first-line ejection-fraction measurement with clinician oversight, although this should be investigated in prospective studies. Funding National Institute for Health and Care Research Clinical Lectureship and the British Heart Foundation Accelerator Award.

title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.
abstract: Background Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival. Methods We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Findings Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p<0·0001 in the training cohort). Multivariate analysis confirmed risk stratification based on the multitask hybrid model score as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. Analysis of patients with stage II or stage III disease in the training cohort and internal and external validation cohorts showed that in those with low predicted scores versus high predicted scores, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in patients with low scores but not those with high scores. In the immunotherapy cohorts, objective response rates were higher for patients with high predicted scores than for those with low predicted scores (54·5% vs 5·6%; p<0·0001 in immunotherapy cohort 1 and 53·1% vs 9·7%; p=0·0010 in immunotherapy cohort 2). Interpretation By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies. Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival.

Methods

We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

Findings

Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p<0·0001 in the training cohort). Multivariate analysis confirmed risk stratification based on the multitask hybrid model score as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. Analysis of patients with stage II or stage III disease in the training cohort and internal and external validation cohorts showed that in those with low predicted scores versus high predicted scores, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in patients with low scores but not those with high scores. In the immunotherapy cohorts, objective response rates were higher for patients with high predicted scores than for those with low predicted scores (54·5% vs 5·6%; p<0·0001 in immunotherapy cohort 1 and 53·1% vs 9·7%; p=0·0010 in immunotherapy cohort 2).

Interpretation

By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in older adults: a scoping review.
abstract: Multimorbidity, non-specific symptoms, and atypical disease manifestations are common in adults aged 65 years or older, complicating diagnostic and prognostic assessment. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) provides real-time bedside imaging that can support clinical decision making in this population; however, evidence on its use in older adults has not been systematically mapped. This scoping Review, endorsed by the European Geriatric Medicine Society, mapped POCUS utilisation across health-care settings, application domains, clinical indications, and outcomes. MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed original research articles investigating the use of POCUS in older adults (defined as studies that exclusively enrolled older adults ≥65 years or reported a mixed-age study population with a mean age of 65 years or older) and published in English or another language represented within the review team (Italian, French, German, Spanish, Danish, or Turkish) with no restrictions on publication date. Of the 3897 records, 240 (6%) studies were included; 87 (36%) focused on older adult or geriatric-targeted populations and 153 (64%) on mixed-age populations with a mean age of 65 years or older. Evidence came predominantly from acute care, with few studies in geriatric settings. Thoracic POCUS was the most frequently investigated single-organ domain; multiorgan POCUS was also prominent. Diagnostic support and prognostic stratification predominated, whereas longitudinal monitoring and patient-centred outcomes were infrequent. Evidence on POCUS applications in older adults remains uneven, highlighting the need for further research in under-represented geriatric care settings and on patient-centred outcomes.

title: Effect of annotation strategy on deep learning-based intracranial hemorrhage segmentation in postmortem computed tomography.
abstract: Postmortem changes may appear as hyperattenuating findings that resemble intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) on postmortem computed tomography (PMCT). This study investigated the effect of two annotation strategies on deep learning-based ICH segmentation in PMCT. Fifty-five pre-autopsy head PMCT cases with autopsy-confirmed ICH were included. Two label sets were created from the same images. The hemorrhage-suspected hyperattenuation (HS) label was based on hyperattenuating findings visible on PMCT without predefined postmortem-specific exclusion criteria. The forensic-reference-guided (FS) label was refined using autopsy records and gross photographs to exclude findings interpreted as non-lesional postmortem changes and correct hemorrhage annotations. These materials provided supportive reference information and were not spatially registered to individual PMCT slices. Two U-Net++ models with a ResNet-34 encoder were trained using the HS and FS labels, respectively, and evaluated by seven-fold case-wise cross-validation. When evaluated against the FS label, the FS model showed higher precision (0.863 vs. 0.665; p < 0.0001) and a lower 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (3.47 vs. 33.79 mm; p = 0.0020), whereas the HS model showed significantly higher recall (0.927 vs. 0.843; p < 0.0001). Dice coefficients did not differ between the models (0.850 [95% CI, 0.611-0.889] vs. 0.746 [95% CI, 0.625-0.790]; p = 0.2027). The HS model produced false-positive predictions around the dural venous sinuses and falx. These findings demonstrate that PMCT-specific annotation changes the learned segmentation target and error profile. Attenuation-based annotation favored broader coverage but more false-positive segmentation of postmortem mimics, whereas forensic-reference-guided annotation produced more selective predictions.
