title: Methylphenidate-associated brain structural changes and neuroimaging predictors of treatment response in youth with ADHD: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Methylphenidate (MPH) is a psychostimulant widely prescribed to children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Although its clinical efficacy is well established, its lasting effects on the developing brain remain unclear. Objective This systematic review aimed to examine associations between long-term MPH treatment and brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD using structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), distinguishing longitudinal treatment-effect studies from cross-sectional medication-history comparisons and baseline neuroimaging predictors of treatment response. Methods A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE and Embase databases. Studies were included if they investigated structural brain changes (gray matter volume, white matter integrity and cortical thickness) after at least four weeks of MPH treatment in children with ADHD. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using the NIH quality assessment tool. Results Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: three longitudinal studies using repeated MRI to assess within-subject treatment effects, two cross-sectional comparisons based on medication history, and three studies using baseline neuroimaging to predict subsequent treatment response. Greater putamen volume was associated with medication status ad volume with better treatment response in the cross-sectional and predictive analyses, while cortical effects were less consistent and mainly age-dependent in frontal areas. White matter findings were subtle and inconsistent across studies, and cortical thickness evidence-limited to one study-suggests short-term, possibly transient effects in children. Conclusion MPH treatment is associated l with age-dependent differences in brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD; however, the limited number of included studies varied substantially in design, (cross-sectional and predictive studies alongside longitudinal treatment-effect studies), methodology, and reported outcomes, making firm causal conclusions difficult. Future research should prioritize larger, standardized, long-term longitudinal studies that account for developmental factors.

originalAbstract:
Background

Methylphenidate (MPH) is a psychostimulant widely prescribed to children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Although its clinical efficacy is well established, its lasting effects on the developing brain remain unclear.

Objective

This systematic review aimed to examine associations between long-term MPH treatment and brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD using structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), distinguishing longitudinal treatment-effect studies from cross-sectional medication-history comparisons and baseline neuroimaging predictors of treatment response.

Methods

A systematic search was conducted in MEDLINE and Embase databases. Studies were included if they investigated structural brain changes (gray matter volume, white matter integrity and cortical thickness) after at least four weeks of MPH treatment in children with ADHD. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed using the NIH quality assessment tool.

Results

Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: three longitudinal studies using repeated MRI to assess within-subject treatment effects, two cross-sectional comparisons based on medication history, and three studies using baseline neuroimaging to predict subsequent treatment response. Greater putamen volume was associated with medication status ad volume with better treatment response in the cross-sectional and predictive analyses, while cortical effects were less consistent and mainly age-dependent in frontal areas. White matter findings were subtle and inconsistent across studies, and cortical thickness evidence-limited to one study-suggests short-term, possibly transient effects in children.

Conclusion

MPH treatment is associated l with age-dependent differences in brain structure in children and adolescents with ADHD; however, the limited number of included studies varied substantially in design, (cross-sectional and predictive studies alongside longitudinal treatment-effect studies), methodology, and reported outcomes, making firm causal conclusions difficult. Future research should prioritize larger, standardized, long-term longitudinal studies that account for developmental factors.

title: Multisystem assessment of white matter tracts in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis using NODDI and TractSeg.
abstract: Background Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a multisystem neurodegenerative disorder affecting motor, cognitive, and sensory networks. Conventional diffusion MRI lacks specificity for complex white matter pathology. This study combined neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) with automated fiber segmentation (TractSeg) to systematically evaluate microstructural alterations across multiple white matter pathways in a single ALS cohort. Methods We combined NODDI with automated TractSeg fiber segmentation in 83 sporadic ALS patients and 59 healthy controls. NODDI metrics (NDI, ODI, ISOVF) were extracted from 98 nodes along 19 tracts. Group comparisons used ANCOVA with FDR correction (q < 0.05). Results The left corticospinal tract (CST) showed ODI elevation and NDI reduction, and the right CST showed more extensive injury with ODI elevation, widespread NDI reduction, and ISOVF elevation. The corpus callosum exhibited focal changes in the rostral body, the anterior midbody and the posterior midbody involving ODI, NDI, and ISOVF. Among cerebellar motor, visuospatial processing, and limbic pathways, only the right superior longitudinal fasciculus II showed ISOVF elevation. Visual and language pathways predominantly showed ISOVF elevation, with additional NDI elevation in the right optic radiation and left arcuate fasciculus. Conclusions This study demonstrates asymmetric, pathway-selective white matter pathology in ALS. Focal damage in the mid-body of the corpus callosum supports its role as a hub for interhemispheric disease propagation. Evidence of both degeneration and possible compensatory neurite reorganization in visual and language pathways further establishes ALS as a multisystem network disorder. NODDI combined with TractSeg offers biologically specific imaging biomarkers for disease monitoring and clinical subtyping.

title: In vivo probabilistic atlas mapping reveals brainstem nuclei volume increases in idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder.
abstract: Objective Idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) serves as a key prodromal marker of synucleinopathies, and its core symptoms are closely associated with brainstem pathology. Nevertheless, in vivo imaging research on brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients is still limited due to methodological constraints. This study aimed to explore volume changes of brainstem nuclei in iRBD patients via a fine-grained probabilistic atlas, and analyze their clinical correlations and diagnostic value. Methods We enrolled 3D T1-weighted MRI data of 178 iRBD patients and 111 healthy controls from the PPMI database. After preprocessing, 54 brainstem nuclei were segmented using the Brainstem Navigator atlas, and their relative volumes were compared between groups with multiple comparison correction. Correlation analyses with clinical scales and ROC analyses were conducted for nuclei with significant inter-group differences. Results Compared to HCs, iRBD patients presented significantly enlarged relative volumes in the left cuneiform nucleus, left lateral parabrachial nucleus, and left superior medullary reticular formation. The volumes of the latter two nuclei were positively correlated with RBDSQ scores and related to autonomic, affective and cognitive indicators. The AUC of single nucleus for iRBD diagnosis ranged from 0.607 to 0.637, while the combined model reached 0.674. Conclusion These findings confirm volumetric enlargement in specific brainstem nuclei of iRBD patients, suggesting early pathological remodeling in these regions. They clarify the brainstem structural basis of iRBD symptoms and suggest that brainstem nuclei volumes, with moderate discriminative performance, may serve as supplementary imaging markers to complement clinical assessments in iRBD.

title: Relationship between integrated myocardial flow reserve and obstructive coronary artery disease and major adverse cardiac events: Findings from the multicenter REFINE PET Registry.
abstract: Introduction Although myocardial flow reserve (MFR) is a powerful marker of prognosis in patients undergoing positron emission tomography myocardial perfusion imaging (PET MPI), MFR cannot distinguish between epicardial and microvascular disease. Integrated MFR (iMFR) has been proposed to better detect epicardial coronary artery disease (CAD) by combining MFR with focal perfusion abnormalities. Methods We studied 34,761 patients as part of the REFINE PET registry of patients undergoing 82Rb or 13N-ammonia PET MPI. A subset of the above population without prior CAD (N=2,869) had a diagnostic angiogram within 180 days of PET MPI. Regions with an MFR <2 and a regional perfusion defect by total perfusion deficit (TPD) were defined as 'focally impaired' on a pixel by pixel basis. Regions with an MFR <2 without a regional perfusion defect were defined as 'diffusely impaired'. We also evaluated a separate angiographic cohort imaged with a third tracer, 18F-flurpiridaz, in the Flurpiridaz-301 trial (N=231). iMFR metrics were evaluated for the prediction of obstructive CAD and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Results Of the 34,761 registry patients, 9,782 (28%) experienced MACE over a median follow-up of 3.8 years. In the angiographic cohort, 1,597 of 2,869 patients (56%) had obstructive CAD. For the diagnosis of obstructive CAD, the extent of focally impaired myocardium had an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.75-0.79), outperforming conventional minimal-segment MFR (AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.74, P<0.001), but did not differ significantly from ischemic TPD or physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided the most prognostic information in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 1.32-1.38; C-statistic 0.723), compared with global MFR (C-statistic 0.722) and focally impaired myocardium (C-statistic 0.711). Conclusion The extent of focally impaired myocardium by iMFR outperformed conventional MFR for the diagnosis of obstructive CAD but performed similarly to ischemic TPD and physician visual scoring. For the prediction of MACE, the extent of diffusely impaired myocardium provided more prognostic information than focally impaired myocardium or global MFR.

title: Influence of preoperative and intraoperative variables on refractive error in patients undergoing phacovitrectomy.
abstract: Phacovitrectomy has been associated with a postoperative myopic shift, potentially resulting from inaccuracies in intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation due to anatomical changes following vitrectomy. This study evaluated postoperative refractive error (RE) and identified pre- and intraoperative factors influencing refractive outcomes after phacovitrectomy. A retrospective review of 311 patients who underwent uncomplicated phacovitrectomy between October 2022 and December 2023 was performed. Preoperative variables included demographic characteristics, diagnosis, axial length, keratometry, anterior chamber depth, biometry method, and IOL calculation formula. Tamponade type was recorded intraoperatively. The primary outcome was RE, defined as the postoperative achieved spherical equivalent (SE) minus the predicted SE based on the implanted IOL power, measured at 1 and 3 months. The mean postoperative SE was -0.828 ± 1.045 D at 1 month and -0.840 ± 0.981 D at 3 months. Mean RE was -0.544 D and -0.556 D, respectively, with no significant difference between visits (p = 0.756). Nearly half of patients (48.5%) had a myopic shift greater than -0.50 D. Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) showed the greatest myopic shift (-1.026 D). The combination of optical biometry and Barrett Universal II was associated with lower RE than ultrasound biometry and SRK/T (p < 0.05). Tamponade type showed no significant association with RE. Phacovitrectomy was associated with a consistent postoperative myopic shift. The combination of optical biometry and Barrett Universal II provided greater refractive accuracy. Patients with RRD showed a greater tendency toward myopic shift. These findings support a more individualized approach to optimize refractive outcomes following phacovitrectomy.

title: A Teleglaucoma Screening System for Individuals at Risk of Open-Angle Glaucoma: Long-Term Clinical Outcomes and Comparative Cost Analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of a teleglaucoma screening program for individuals at increased risk of developing open-angle glaucoma (OAG). Design Prospective cohort study with retrospective evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes and comparative cost analysis. Participants Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG enrolled in a teleglaucoma screening program between 2020 and 2022. Methods A targeted teleglaucoma screening program was implemented within the Donostialdea Integrated Healthcare Organization (Gipuzkoa, Spain). Consecutive individuals with risk factors for OAG were included. The teleglaucoma assessment included best-corrected visual acuity, non-contact tonometry, pachymetry, and peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer optical coherence tomography (pRNFL-OCT), performed by an optometrist and reviewed asynchronously by glaucoma specialists. Findings consistent with glaucoma or suspicious for glaucoma were considered positive screening results, whereas ocular hypertension (OHT) or the absence of abnormalities were considered negative screening results. Clinical effectiveness was evaluated through analysis of glaucoma-related diagnoses recorded using ICD-10 codes during a five-year follow-up period. A comparative cost analysis was conducted from a societal perspective. Patient satisfaction was assessed using the Client Satisfaction Questionnaire (CSQ-8). Main outcomes measures Agreement between teleglaucoma classifications and glaucoma-related ICD-10 diagnoses recorded during follow-up, diagnostic performance indicators, patient satisfaction, and costs. Results A total of 1,112 patients were included (mean age 60.2 years), of whom 63.1% were women. Positive screening results were identified in 8.2% of participants. Overall agreement between the teleglaucoma assessment and follow-up ICD-10 diagnoses was 92.6%, with a mean follow-up of 3.7 ± 0.8 years. Sensitivity was 64.5%, specificity 93.4%, and negative predictive value 98.9%. Patient satisfaction was high, with a mean score of 8.5/10. The economic analysis demonstrated a 50% reduction in total costs compared with conventional care, with a cost per patient of €40.7 versus €81.2. Conclusions The teleglaucoma system demonstrated a high ability to rule out disease among individuals at risk of glaucoma, reduced costs and achieved high patient satisfaction. However, moderate sensitivity and the use of coded clinical records as the reference standard should be considered.

title: External validation of a deep-learning algorithm for perimetric glaucoma detection on color fundus photographs in the Rotterdam Study.
abstract: Purpose To externally validate a deep-learning (DL) algorithm detecting perimetric glaucoma on color fundus photographs (CFPs) in a population-based cohort. Design External validation in a prospective population-based cohort. Participants Participants aged 50-80 years from three Rotterdam Study cohorts. Methods We applied the winning Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening (AIROGS) challenge algorithm, trained on 101,442 macula-centered CFPs to detect referable presumed perimetric glaucoma. Performance was assessed at eye and participant level, with participant-level cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Misclassified cases underwent qualitative review. Longitudinal detection was evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. Additionally, paired analyses compared macula- with disc-centered CFPs. A post-hoc analysis examined the effect of image quality on positive predictive value (PPV). Main outcome measures Sensitivity at 95% specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC), partial AUC (pAUC) for 90-100% specificity, PPV, and precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC). Results Among 19,088 eyes (9,837 participants), 201 eyes (1.1%) had perimetric glaucoma. At eye level, sensitivity at 95% specificity was 70.6% (95% CI: 63.8-76.8), with an ROC-AUC of 0.911 (95% CI: 0.887-0.934) and a PR-AUC of 0.343 (95% CI: 0.274-0.427). At participant level, sensitivity was 68.8% (95% CI: 61.8-75.9) and ROC-AUC 0.909 (95% CI: 0.882-0.934). Overall, this resulted in 5.1 referrals per detected glaucoma case. True positives showed more advanced visual field damage than false negatives (median mean deviation -10.8 vs -5.8 dB; P < 0.001). Among true positives with prior imaging, 33 of 61 (54%) were flagged before conversion, typically 4-7 years before diagnosis. Discrimination in the 90-100% specificity range was higher for disc- than macula-centered CFPs (pAUC 0.860 vs 0.802; P = 0.003). PPV improved substantially after excluding CFPs with incomplete optic nerve head (ONH) visibility. Conclusions The DL-algorithm achieved meaningful discrimination for perimetric glaucoma in an external population-based dataset. Correctly identified cases were frequently flagged at an earlier examination, years before the perimetric diagnosis. Despite having been trained exclusively on macula-centered CFPs, the DL-algorithm showed no loss of discriminative performance on disc-centered CFPs. Incomplete ONH visibility was an important source of false positives. These findings support CFP-based deep learning as a scalable triage tool for glaucoma screening and highlight image acquisition standards for implementation.

title: Diagnostic orthodontic traction with a miniscrew for stacked horizontal impaction of the mandibular second and third molars followed by fixed orthodontic appliance involving premolar extractions in a young adult presenting with Class II incisal biprotrusion: A case report.
abstract: Stacked horizontal impaction of the mandibular second and third molars presents complex clinical challenges because of uncertainty regarding tooth preservation, uprighting mechanics, and the possibility of ankylosis. A 23-year-old male presented with a skeletal Class II malocclusion, excessive overjet, and moderate crowding. Radiographic examination revealed stacked horizontal impactions of the left mandibular second and third molars. To evaluate the orthodontic responsiveness of the impacted mandibular left second molar before irreversible extraction decisions were made, diagnostic orthodontic traction using a miniscrew was performed. Following extraction of the mandibular left third molar, a miniscrew was placed distal to the impacted second molar to initiate orthodontic traction. This diagnostic approach confirmed responsiveness of the impacted second molar to orthodontic force and guided definitive treatment planning. Once orthodontic tooth movement had been confirmed, the mandibular left second premolar were extracted, allowing mesial movement of the mandibular left first molar and successful uprighting of the impacted second molar. A stable Class I molar relationship and functional occlusion were achieved. Clinical and radiographic evaluation after a 2-year retention period demonstrated excellent occlusal stability and healthy periodontal conditions. This case demonstrates that diagnostic orthodontic traction using a miniscrew can provide a useful staged decision-making strategy for managing severely impacted mandibular second molar with uncertain prognosis.

title: Quantitative 3D mapping of the integrated sweat duct-microvasculature unit via fingerprint-guided photoacoustic/ultrasound microscopy.
abstract: Cutaneous thermoregulation relies on coordinated interactions between sweat ducts and the dermal microvasculature. However, single-modality imaging cannot simultaneously visualize and characterize this functional coupling. Here, we present a fingerprint-guided dual-modal photoacoustic/ultrasound (PA/US) microscopy framework for three-dimensional mapping of the integrated sweat duct-microvasculature unit (SDMU). This strategy combines high-frequency ultrasound with deep learning (U-Net) to extract sweat duct and fingerprint features; simultaneously, the distribution of microvasculature in PA imaging is accurately localized via structural similarity index metrix (SSIM) analysis of depth-dependent melanin. Crucially, fingerprint-guided non-rigid registration eliminates motion artifacts, enabling dynamic tracking of the identical SDMUs during physiological processes. Quantitative analysis indicated that the functional coupling of microvasculature is highly concentrated within a 75-micrometer radius around sweat ducts, and that the expansion of US-visible sweat ductal structures exhibits a strong positive correlation with microvascular recruitment. Furthermore, a physiology-informed operational dual-response criterion further revealed significant spatial heterogeneity in functional activation, thereby facilitating robust discrimination between activated and unactivated SDMUs. This study not only established the SDMU as a quantifiable functional unit for studying cutaneous thermoregulation, but also highlighted its potential as a candidate biomarker for assessing diabetes-associated neurovascular dysfunction.

title: Hyperspectral Histopathology with Spectral-Spatial Multiple-Instance Learning for Acute Leukemia Classification.
abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) may show overlapping morphology on bone-marrow trephine sections, while definitive ancillary testing is not always immediately available. We evaluated whether microscopic hyperspectral imaging (HSI) combined with patient-level spectral-spatial deep learning could support differentiation of AML, ALL, and normal marrow. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 78 patients (26 AML, 26 ALL, and 26 normal marrow). H&E-stained bone-marrow trephine sections were imaged across 400-1000 nm. Patient-level nested stratified five-fold cross-validation was defined before region-of-interest (ROI) sampling to prevent information leakage. We developed HemaSpec-MIL, a new hierarchical spectral-spatial multiple-instance learning algorithm and a major methodological output of this study. The framework combines multi-scale spectral encoding, morphology encoding, bidirectional cross-attention, and gated multiple-instance aggregation to generate patient-level probabilities. The primary endpoint was pooled out-of-fold macro-AUC. Results HemaSpec-MIL achieved a pooled out-of-fold accuracy of 0.897, macro-F1 of 0.897, and macro-AUC of 0.957. One-vs-rest AUCs were 0.964 for AML, 0.945 for ALL, and 0.962 for normal marrow. Performance exceeded spectral-only, morphology-only, 3D-CNN, Vision Transformer, and spectral Transformer baselines. Ablation analysis supported complementary contributions from the spectral branch, morphology branch, cross-attention fusion, gated patient-level aggregation, and spectral augmentation. Conclusions Microscopic HSI combined with the newly developed HemaSpec-MIL framework enabled accurate internal differentiation of AML, ALL, and normal marrow while preserving wavelength- and tissue-level interpretability. Independent multicenter validation and acquisition harmonization are required before clinical translation.

title: Association of Scanning Laser Ophthalmoscopy-Derived Fundus Metrics with Corneal Remodeling after Transepithelial Photorefractive Keratectomy: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the associations between preoperative fundus metrics and postoperative corneal remodeling following transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK). Methods This retrospective observational study included 103 patients (200 eyes) who underwent TransPRK. Corneal parameters were measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. A screening strategy using two standardized metrics, A = SD(Δ)/SD(T₀) and B = median(|Δ|)/SD(T₀), was implemented to identify high-variability corneal parameters, where Δ denotes the change from preoperative baseline, SD(Δ) the standard deviation of the change, and SD(T₀) the preoperative standard deviation of the same parameter. Patient-clustered generalized estimating equation (GEE) models adjusted for age, sex, preoperative spherical equivalent (SE), and preoperative corneal epithelial thickness (CET) were used to examine the associations between retained corneal parameters and preoperative fundus metrics, including fundus tessellation density (FTD), parapapillary atrophy (PPA) area, vertical cup-to-disc ratio (VCDR), and rim-to-disc area ratio (RDAR). The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. Results Twenty-seven corneal parameters were identified as high-variability parameters, most showing their greatest change at 1 month postoperatively. VCDR was positively associated with changes in TNP K1 and TCRP K1 (standardized β = 0.065 to 0.076), and these associations remained significant after BH correction at both 1 and 3 months (all q < 0.05). RDAR was negatively associated with the same parameters in these generalized estimating equation (GEE) models (standardized β = -0.071 to -0.060) and remained significant at 3 months postoperatively (q < 0.05); PPA area and FTD were not significantly associated with any corneal parameter. Conclusions Preoperative VCDR was significantly associated with corneal changes after TransPRK, independent of surgical parameters, whereas the association for RDAR was partly attenuated after adjustment. These findings suggest that posterior segment structure may influence anterior corneal remodeling through biomechanical pathways, though further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Changes in Retinal and Choroidal Thickness and OCTA-Derived Vessel Density after Anti-VEGF Therapy for Diabetic Macular Edema.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the effects of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapy on retinal and choroidal thickness and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)-derived retinal vessel density in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME), with prespecified primary outcomes and exploratory OCTA outcomes controlled for multiplicity. Methods This retrospective clinical study included 45 patients (45 eyes) with DME treated at the Affiliated Eye Hospital of Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine between January 2023 and January 2026. All patients received three consecutive monthly intravitreal injections of conbercept (0.5 mg/0.05 mL). OCTA examinations were performed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months after the first injection to measure central macular thickness (CMT), subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus (SCP) and deep capillary plexus (DCP), foveal avascular zone (FAZ) area, and parafoveal vessel density at 300 μm (FD-300). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was also recorded. BCVA, CMT, and SFCT were prespecified as primary outcomes. All OCTA-derived parameters were exploratory and were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure across 12 comparisons. Results The study included 45 patients (45 eyes), comprising 21 male patients (21 eyes) and 24 female patients (24 eyes), with a mean age of 54.44 ± 12.09 years. The mean duration of diabetes was 13.33 ± 4.36 years, and the baseline HbA1c level was 7.36% ± 1.73%. At 3 months, BCVA significantly improved from 0.65 ± 0.45 to 0.33 ± 0.27 logMAR (P < 0.001). CMT significantly decreased from 392.02 ± 139.90 μm at baseline to 322.26 ± 85.60 μm at 3 months (P = 0.002 vs baseline; overall P = 0.006). SFCT significantly decreased from 260.51 ± 106.16 μm at baseline to 243.80 ± 91.15 μm at 3 months (P = 0.020 vs baseline; overall P = 0.037). In exploratory OCTA analyses, foveal SCP and DCP vessel density showed numerical increases at 3 months (SCP: 26.88 ± 6.71% to 29.94 ± 7.32%; DCP: 30.02 ± 6.46% to 33.54 ± 6.74%), with uncorrected main-effect P values of 0.041 and 0.043, respectively. However, neither remained statistically significant after FDR correction (adjusted P = 0.224 and 0.256, respectively). No significant changes were observed in parafoveal SCP or DCP vessel density, FAZ area, or FD-300 (all FDR-adjusted P > 0.05). No serious adverse events occurred. Conclusion Anti-VEGF therapy significantly improved BCVA and reduced CMT and SFCT over 3 months. Foveal SCP and DCP vessel density increased numerically, but these exploratory OCTA changes did not survive FDR correction and may reflect edema-resolution-related segmentation effects; they are hypothesis-generating only. Longer prospective studies with standardized OCTA metrics are needed.

Anti-VEGF therapy significantly improved BCVA and reduced CMT and SFCT over 3 months. Foveal SCP and DCP vessel density increased numerically, but these exploratory OCTA changes did not survive FDR correction and may reflect edema-resolution-related segmentation effects; they are hypothesis-generating only. Longer prospective studies with standardized OCTA metrics are needed.

title: Functional lung avoidance planning with combined ventilation-perfusion imaging versus individual functional imaging in lung cancer radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Functional lung avoidance radiotherapy using four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) ventilation or single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) perfusion has been studied independently, however few studies have evaluated their combined use. The aim of this study was to examine whether integrating both modalities improved sparing of high functional lung (HFL) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Materials and methods Forty-seven patients with NSCLC underwent 4DCT ventilation and SPECT perfusion imaging. One patient was excluded, leaving 46 for analysis. Functional lung maps were segmented into high, middle, and low functional lung. Four volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plans using 6 MV photons per patient were generated: anatomical (A), ventilation-guided (V), perfusion-guided (Q), and combined ventilation-perfusion-guided (VQ). Dose-volume and dose-function metrics were compared among plans. Correlations between tumor proximity to HFL and dose reduction were assessed. Results All function-guided plans significantly reduced HFL dose compared with A plans ( p < 0.001). Among the function-guided plans, VQ plans yielded the lowest mean lung doses (MLDs) in high ventilated lung (VQ plans, 11.5 Gy; A plans, 12.4 Gy) and high perfused lung (VQ plans, 10.0 Gy; A plans, 11.1 Gy). Function-weighted metrics, including functional MLD, were also lowest with VQ plans, indicating improved functional lung sparing. Dose reduction correlated with tumor proximity to HFL, with the strongest associations observed at planning target volume expansions between 25 and 45 mm. Conclusions Integrating 4DCT ventilation and SPECT perfusion into radiotherapy planning improved functional lung sparing compared with anatomical or single-modality planning. Tumor proximity to functional lung influenced the magnitude of dose-volume benefits.

title: Bayesian deep learning framework to address multi-rater annotation uncertainty in prostate cancer magnetic resonance imaging segmentation.
abstract: Background and purpose Accurate prostate segmentation in magnetic resonance imaging is critical for prostate cancer radiotherapy, but manual annotation is time-consuming and exhibits high inter-rater variability. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning framework that improves prostate segmentation under annotation noise and inter-rater variability while providing uncertainty estimation. Materials and methods Using the prostate cancer imaging dataset (140 subjects), simulated prostate annotations modeled boundary ambiguity, annotator subjectivity, and annotation tool-related artifacts across three scenarios: single rater with distinct simulated annotations (S1), majority-vote consensus from three raters (S2), and multi-annotation of all rater masks with majority voting (S3). The framework used Flipout convolutional layers for uncertainty estimation, trained with a combined Kullback-Leibler divergence and Focal Tversky loss. Bayesian learning was implemented first in a standard U-Net and then in nnU-Net to evaluate generalization across backbones. Comparisons included deterministic counterparts, Swin UNETR, and variants with Monte Carlo Dropout, Label Smoothing, and Test-Time Augmentation. Results Bayesian U-Net achieved Dice Similarity Coefficients of 0.730, 0.782, and 0.780 in S1, S2, and S3, respectively, and the lowest Expected Calibration Error in S1 (0.065). Bayesian nnU-Net achieved the highest Dice Similarity Coefficients among nnU-Net-based methods in all scenarios (0.879, 0.903, and 0.900) and the lowest Expected Calibration Error in all scenarios. Predictive uncertainty was consistently higher in incorrectly than in correctly segmented voxels. Conclusions Bayesian learning improved segmentation robustness under multi-rater noisy labels, across both U-Net and nnU-Net while providing voxel-wise uncertainty estimates and may support clinical decision-making and enhance treatment accuracy.

title: Treatment-position magnetic resonance imaging reduces bony-landmark co-registration error in head and neck radiotherapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Routine diagnostic magnetic resonance imaging is acquired without immobilisation, creating co-registration uncertainty with planning computed tomography. We quantified whether treatment-position imaging reduced bony-landmark co-registration error, and whether the benefit persisted after resampling and deformable refinement. Materials and methods Fifty patients with paired treatment-position and diagnostic magnetic resonance imaging were retrospectively analysed. Each magnetic resonance imaging dataset was separately registered to planning computed tomography. Mean Euclidean distance between corresponding bony landmarks on the computed tomography and magnetic resonance images was compared after rigid registration and after deformable refinement, using Holm-adjusted landmark-wise comparisons. Through-plane resampling was assessed in all 50 patients, and interobserver reproducibility in a 15-patient subset. Results Treatment-position imaging reduced mean Euclidean distance from 7.5 to 4.1 mm after rigid registration (difference 3.4 mm; 95% confidence interval 2.7-4.1; p = 2.0 × 10 -13 ). The benefit persisted after resampling (4.3 mm) and deformable refinement (3.4 versus 6.0 mm; difference 2.6 mm; 95% confidence interval 2.1-3.1; p = 7.1 × 10 -14 ), although refinement reduced the advantage by 0.8 mm (interaction p = 0.023). Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.81 for diagnostic imaging and 0.48 for treatment-position imaging (95% confidence interval - 0.05-0.79), with small mean bias and lower treatment-position error in all 15 patients. Conclusions Treatment-position magnetic resonance imaging reduced bony-landmark error in co-registration with planning computed tomography after rigid registration, and the benefit persisted after deformable refinement. Because delineation and dose-volume parameters were not assessed, these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating improved contouring accuracy.

title: Quantitative static contrast-enhanced phantom study to establish performance of advanced cone beam computed tomography for functional imaging applications.
abstract: Background and purpose Dynamic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (DCE-CT) is a quantitative imaging technique that measures vascular perfusion. Extending this to cone beam CT (CBCT) would enable functional measurements on radiotherapy machines. An advanced CBCT imaging solution, with enhanced image quality and rapid acquisitions, offers potential. However, the static quantitative and spatial performance of advanced CBCT relevant to DCE imaging has not been characterized. Materials and methods To address this, the image quality of advanced CBCT was compared with standard CBCT and CT using contrast-enhanced phantoms with DCE-specific characteristics not previously applied to CBCT. A contrast enhancement CT (CECT) phantom (acrylic cylinder with capsule inserts) and a humanoid phantom (human torso with a liver containing tumour-mimicking spheres) were imaged across different acquisition settings. Results Using the CECT phantom, advanced CBCT demonstrated improved CT number accuracy compared to standard CBCT (<23.9 vs. <78.9 HU) and greater CT number constancy (<8.4 vs. <12.9 HU). Iterative reconstruction on advanced CBCT offered improvements over filtered back-projection. Using the humanoid phantom, findings were confirmed with CT number accuracy (<7.1 vs. <42.8 HU), CT number variation (<11.3 vs. <49.8 HU) and volume accuracy (<128.8 vs. <1067.3 mm 3 ). Advanced CBCT achieved spatial resolutions of 2.3-5.0 lp/cm across different acquisitions and measurements, meeting the 5 lp/cm clinical benchmark under certain conditions. It also displayed stable CT number-density calibration. Conclusions Advanced CBCT compared to standard CBCT improved image quality, approaching CT-level performance. Findings demonstrated robust volume and contrast-specific quantification under DCE conditions, supporting further evaluation of functional CBCT.

title: Quantitative gamma-based evaluation of a novel four-dimensional computed tomography reconstruction algorithm for stack artifact reduction.
abstract: Background and purpose Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is essential for motion-resolved imaging in radiotherapy, but stack alignment artifacts caused by irregular breathing may compromise anatomical accuracy. This study established a quantitative framework to evaluate reconstruction differences between clinical reference reconstruction (CRR) and stack artifact-reduced reconstruction (SARR) and identify clinically relevant changes. Materials and methods Retrospective 4DCT datasets from 80 lung cancer patients were analyzed, comprising a rated cohort ( n = 30) and an independent control cohort ( n = 50). Geometric, intensity-based, and combined metrics, including gamma analysis, were calculated across ten respiratory phases for segmented organs-at-risk. Correlations with reader ratings identified metrics that best reflected clinically relevant reconstruction differences. Results Most similarity and intensity-based measures showed limited association with image quality differences (Pearson correlation coefficient r < 0.5). Gamma-based metrics demonstrated the strongest correlation, with relative gamma area > 0.3 reaching r ≈ 0.59 for phase-based data (95% confidence interval 0.30-0.79). Reconstruction differences were predominantly observed in the liver and lower lung lobes, consistent with respiratory motion, while the spinal cord showed minimal variation. Robust z-score thresholding enabled automated categorization of moderate and substantial deviations. In the control cohort, 12% showed substantial and 14% moderate changes for phase-based reconstructions. In the patient with the largest changes, the liver appeared as a double contour in the CRR and as a single contour in the SARR. Conclusions Gamma-based evaluation provided an objective method to detect and localize reconstruction differences in 4DCT, supporting transparent clinical implementation of advanced reconstruction algorithms in radiotherapy.

title: MRI-based radiomics and deep learning for the prenatal diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
abstract: Objective accuracy of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) diagnosis using conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is still limited by subjective interpretation. Increasing evidence showed that radiomics and Deep Learning (DL) may improve diagnostic objectivity by extracting quantitative features from MRI data. This study aimed to synthesize the evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of these models. Methods a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines and PRISMA 2020 recommendations: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from inception to December 2025. We searched for primary studies evaluating MRI-based radiomics or DL models for the binary diagnosis of PAS. Data were extracted to create 2 × 2 contingency tables and used a bivariate random-effects model to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, and to generate a summary ROC (SROC) curve. We assessed robustness via leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and clinical utility using Fagan's nomogram and likelihood ratios. A secondary meta-analysis was performed for the prediction of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) ≥1000 mL. Results twelve studies met the inclusion criteria (N = 1135 patients). The pooled sensitivity for PAS diagnosis was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89) and pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88). The summary AUC was 0.896, confirming high diagnostic accuracy. The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 4.61 and the negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.21. Subgroup analyses based on AI model type (p > 0.05) and study design (p > 0.05) did not find significant differences between groups but revealed that single-center studies tended to report higher accuracy compared to multicenter studies. The secondary meta-analysis on massive PPH prediction (n = 4 studies, N = 353 patients: 165 PPH+ and 188 PPH-) yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.63-0.97), a pooled specificity of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.50-0.93), and an AUC of 0.901. originalAbstract:
Objective

accuracy of Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) diagnosis using conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is still limited by subjective interpretation. Increasing evidence showed that radiomics and Deep Learning (DL) may improve diagnostic objectivity by extracting quantitative features from MRI data. This study aimed to synthesize the evidence on the diagnostic performance and clinical utility of these models.

Methods

a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA-DTA guidelines and PRISMA 2020 recommendations: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from inception to December 2025. We searched for primary studies evaluating MRI-based radiomics or DL models for the binary diagnosis of PAS. Data were extracted to create 2 × 2 contingency tables and used a bivariate random-effects model to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, and to generate a summary ROC (SROC) curve. We assessed robustness via leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, and clinical utility using Fagan's nomogram and likelihood ratios. A secondary meta-analysis was performed for the prediction of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) ≥1000 mL.

Results

twelve studies met the inclusion criteria (N = 1135 patients). The pooled sensitivity for PAS diagnosis was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89) and pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88). The summary AUC was 0.896, confirming high diagnostic accuracy. The positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 4.61 and the negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.21. Subgroup analyses based on AI model type (p > 0.05) and study design (p > 0.05) did not find significant differences between groups but revealed that single-center studies tended to report higher accuracy compared to multicenter studies. The secondary meta-analysis on massive PPH prediction (n = 4 studies, N = 353 patients: 165 PPH+ and 188 PPH-) yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.63-0.97), a pooled specificity of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.50-0.93), and an AUC of 0.901.

Conclusions

MRI-based AI models demonstrate high exploratory pooled accuracy for the prenatal diagnosis of PAS in high-risk cohorts. These results suggest that these tools show promising exploratory accuracy and may provide decision support as an adjunct ("human-in-the-loop") in equivocal cases. However, their real-world clinical generalizability remains constrained by retrospective designs and index test threshold optimization.

title: Advances in retinal cellular imaging: Towards single-cell resolution and functional biomarkers.
abstract: Retinal imaging has traditionally described tissue and layer level pathology, whereas direct assessment of individual cells in the living human retina has been limited by ocular aberrations, optical contrast and image analysis constraints. Adaptive optics (AO) has substantially changed this landscape by improving lateral resolution and enabling in vivo visualization of photoreceptors, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), ganglion-cell-layer structures, immune cells and microvasculature. This review discusses human retinal cellular imaging across three major AO-enhanced platforms: flood-illumination adaptive optics (FIAO), adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) and adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO). These modalities provide complementary capabilities, including rapid en face imaging, depth-resolved volumetric assessment and flexible confocal, non-confocal and fluorescence-based contrast. Recent progress is also being shaped by faster wavefront correction, wider-field acquisition, compressed multichannel imaging, sensorless AO and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted reconstruction, segmentation and quantification. Beyond optical resolution, molecular labeling strategies are beginning to add biological specificity to retinal cellular imaging. Indocyanine green (ICG) supports AO-assisted assessment of RPE mosaic contrast, annexin V-based Detection of Apoptosing Retinal Cells (DARC) provides a molecular readout of retinal cell stress and apoptosis, and curcumin-based imaging has been explored as an experimental retinal amyloid marker in Alzheimer's disease. Together, these advances indicate a shift from high-resolution visualization alone towards cellular and molecular biomarkers of disease activity, progression and treatment response. Further translation will require standardized acquisition, robust automated analysis, multimodal validation and larger prospective studies across devices, disease populations and clinical sites.

title: Dual-phase deep learning recommendation system for radiographic crown lengthening assessment and post selection for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth.
abstract: Statement of problem Restoring endodontically treated teeth requires careful evaluation of the supracrestal tissue attachment, ferrule integrity, and post-space dimensions to ensure long-term success. Manual radiographic analysis for crown lengthening indication and post selection is often time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings where specialist access may be constrained. Purpose The purpose of this study was to design and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system that automated 2 essential restorative planning tasks, evaluating the clinical need for crown lengthening and recommending appropriate post dimensions in endodontically treated teeth, using dental radiographs as the input. Material and methods Two deep learning pipelines were developed and trained on annotated panoramic and periapical datasets with annotations created under the supervision of dentistry professionals. The crown measurement pipeline employed a U-shaped network (U-Net) model for initial tooth segmentation (assigning unique instance masks to each tooth), then cropping individual teeth and feeding them into a Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for precise detection and crown length calculation, facilitating the assessment of parameters such as supracrestal tissue attachment and ferrule height, for identification of potential violations or restoration limitations. The post measurement pipeline utilized Mask R-CNN directly on the original images to detect endodontic posts and measure their length and width, enabling comparison against established prosthodontic criteria. Both models were trained in a graphics processing unit (GPU)-enabled environment (Kaggle; Google LLC) and evaluated using standard metrics including Intersection over Union (IoU), Dice coefficient, and measurement accuracy, with validation involving visual overlays and quantitative comparisons to expert annotations. Results The segmentation model achieved a mean IoU of 0.52 and a Dice coefficient of 0.66, with diagnostic accuracy exceeding 99% in identifying post locations and assessing ferrule presence. The system accurately detected supracrestal tissue attachment violations and provided clinically relevant post dimension recommendations, closely aligning with expert-guided decisions. GPU acceleration reduced model training time by over 70% compared to local central processing unit (CPU)-only workflows. Conclusions The AI-powered system demonstrated promising performance in automating radiographic evaluations critical to restoring endodontically treated teeth. By identifying crown lengthening requirements and suggesting post dimensions, the integrated pipelines supported objective and reproducible treatment planning. This approach may enhance prosthodontic workflows, especially in settings with limited specialist availability, and holds potential for integration into commercial dental imaging platforms.

title: Predicting early EGFR-TKI treatment response in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma from H&E histopathology with weakly supervised multiple-instance learning.
abstract: Background This study sought to construct a deep-learning pipeline using an attention mechanism and multiple-instance learning (MIL) to predict early treatment response to epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) directly from routinely available hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs) of pretreatment tissue in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods We retrospectively obtained clinicopathological data from 100 patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. The model employed ResNet-50 for feature representation and integrated a gated-attention pooling mechanism for feature aggregation at the patient level. This weakly supervised approach did not require pixel-level manual annotations and enabled direct slide-level prediction of early treatment response. Results The proposed gated-attention model attained an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.891 in 5-fold cross-validation, which was numerically higher than those of mean pooling (0.837), max pooling (0.821), ABMIL (0.869), CLAM (0.874), and TransMIL (0.863); however, the difference relative to CLAM did not reach statistical significance (unadjusted P = 0.062). In ablation analyses, replacing gated attention with mean pooling resulted in the largest reduction in AUC (0.054). Patient-level nuclear morphometric profiling revealed that the early adverse response group exhibited larger nuclear areas (78.3 ± 22.1 μm² vs. 62.7 ± 18.4 μm² in the favorable response group), along with elevated nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, nuclear eccentricity, and chromatin texture entropy. Chromatin texture entropy was positively correlated with the model-predicted probability of adverse response (r = 0.58, P < 0.001). Furthermore, the adverse response group displayed a higher frequency of TP53-associated alterations (62.5% vs. 38.3%), which encompassed next-generation sequencing findings and p53 immunohistochemical surrogates. In exploratory analyses, a four-variable clinical model yielded an AUC of 0.792, whereas an integrated model incorporating the multiple instance learning (MIL) risk score demonstrated an apparent AUC of 0.918 in this cohort, warranting further out-of-sample validation. Conclusion This study demonstrates that a lightweight and weakly supervised computational-pathology model can support the early estimation of EGFR-TKI treatment response. This pipeline uses routinely acquired H&E slides without requiring additional tissue sampling, provides biologically interpretable outputs, and may support clinical decision-making in precision oncology.

title: Effectiveness of Upfront Radiotherapy in Central Nervous System Germ Cell Tumors.
abstract: Background and purpose Radiotherapy (RT) is essential for curing central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS-GCTs) except for pure mature teratoma (MT), but the optimal target volume, dose, and timing remain controversial. This study evaluated the benefit of upfront RT in CNS-GCTs. Materials and methods We reviewed CNS-GCT patients under 30-year-old treated from 2015 to 2023. Patients with pure germinomas (PG) received whole-ventricular irradiation (WVI) with tumor bed (TB) boost. Patients with malignant non-germinomatous germ cell tumor (MNGGCT) received WVI or whole-brain irradiation (WBI) with TB boost, with or without craniospinal irradiation (CSI), before or after platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy (CTX). Serum alpha-fetoprotein and human chorionic gonadotropin levels guided diagnosis when histopathology was unavailable. Patients with MT were treated surgically. The primary endpoint was 5-year event-free survival (EFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), neurocognitive outcomes, and endocrinopathy rates. Results Twenty-nine patients were analyzed: 13 PGs, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront RT, 7 MNGGCTs with upfront CTX, and 2 MTs. The median follow-up of these tumors was 6.0, 6.6, 3.7, and 10.3 years, respectively. PGs receiving upfront RT achieved 5-year EFS and OS of 100% and 100%, respectively. For MNGGCTs receiving upfront RT, 5-year EFS and OS was 85.7% and 85.7%, respectively; 1 patient died from post-treatment disease progression. MNGGCTs treated with upfront CTX had 5-year EFS and OS of 41.7% and 60.0%, respectively; 2 patients relapsed (1 died), and 1 died from treatment-related complications. Both MTs remained event-free over 6 years following surgery alone or with Gamma Knife radiosurgery. Conclusions Upfront RT provided excellent outcomes in PGs and may eliminate the need for CTX in those achieving complete response.

abstract: Purpose To characterize divergence among international experts in clinical and planning target volume (CTV/PTV) delineation and resulting treatment plans when all begin from the same standardized gross tumor volume (GTV) and organs-at-risk (OAR) set, in two representative scenarios: HPV-associated oropharyngeal and EBV-associated nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy. Methods A global panel recruited through ASTRO, ESTRO, IAEA, FARO, and regional radiation oncology societies received identical DICOM data for two anonymized cases, comprising an expert-defined GTV (primary GTVp, involved-node GTVn) and a shared OAR set; target delineation and planning were left to participants. Each expert drew CTV1/CTV2 (±CTV3) and PTV1/PTV2/PTV3 and produced a deliverable IMRT/VMAT plan. Contours pooled in ProKnow DS yielded a consensus atlas whose 50% iso-agreement envelope served as the consensus reference. Agreement was scored by matching, missing, and extra volume, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), and mean center-of-mass (COM) displacement in X/Y/Z. Submitted plans were benchmarked against a consensus plan and published dose thresholds. Results Thirty-two experts contributed target delineations (per-structure N 26-32); 25 submitted complete, deliverable plans. CTV1 concordance was moderate-to-high but heterogeneous (oropharynx DSC 0.72 ± 0.19; nasopharynx 0.73 ± 0.19), approximating a GTV + ∼5 mm expansion, and fell for CTV2 (0.66 ± 0.17 and 0.67 ± 0.17). It was lowest for the elective low-dose nasopharyngeal PTV3 (0.45 ± 0.21; extra volume mean 245.5 cc, SD 310.5; COM shift up to ∼17-26 mm). Target coverage was adequate (oropharynx PTV1 D95 mean 69.4 Gy, SD 1.4; nasopharynx 68.7 Gy, SD 2.0). OAR doses, though generally within accepted limits, were heterogeneous: in nasopharynx, dispersion and the gap between the average expert and consensus plan were greatest for the optic apparatus, eyes/lens, cochleae, and brainstem, which the consensus plan spared substantially more than the population average; in oropharynx, dispersion was greatest for the supraglottic larynx, cochlea, brainstem, and spinal canal. Conclusions Even from a standardized GTV, experts did not achieve high agreement in target volumes or plans; disagreement widened in elective nodal coverage and OAR trade-offs. Consensus-based peer review, potentially with AI-assisted contouring and planning guidance, warrants prospective study to reduce interobserver variation and standardize plan optimization and acceptance.

title: Safely Navigating the MR-Linac: A New Risk Framework for Prostate SBRT Patients with Cardiac Devices.
abstract: Purpose Prostate stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) on a 1.5-T magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) linear accelerator (MR-linac) combines high-contrast intrafraction imaging with online adaptive replanning and enables focal dose intensification. Patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) nonetheless face barriers to MR-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT), because existing guidance addresses diagnostic MRI and radiotherapy exposures separately and does not specify fraction-level requirements for their combination. We developed and implemented a framework integrating both domains in one operational pathway. Methods A multidisciplinary group synthesized diagnostic MRI, radiotherapy, and MR-linac safety evidence into a dual-axis risk model. The MRI/CIED axis is keyed to device exposure (generator-lead configuration, manufacturer conditions, and sequence-level radiofrequency and gradient compliance) rather than anatomic field of view. The radiotherapy (RT)/CIED axis stratifies neutron production, cumulative generator dose, generator-to-field geometry, and pacing dependence. A failure mode and effects analysis translated high-priority scenarios into hold points and role assignments; the pathway is implemented prospectively for CIED patients on a 1.5-T MR-linac. Results The two axes intersect in a matrix assigning every patient to one of six classes: LOW, LOW/INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE, INTERMEDIATE/HIGH, HIGH, or HOLD. Each class specifies monitoring, consent, interrogation, programming, personnel, and platform requirements. These are implemented through a day-of-treatment workflow with named role ownership and sequential hold points aligned with the 2026 American College of Radiology Manual on MR Safety. Two determinations override the matrix: MR-hold defers MRgRT irrespective of radiotherapy category, and RT-high defaults to computed tomography-guided radiotherapy. Conclusions By unifying MRI- and radiotherapy-specific device risks, the dual-axis framework converts categorical CIED exclusion into a graded, prospectively assigned disposition and makes every decision auditable. It is in prospective clinical use and offers appropriately selected patients a conservative route to MRgRT and the documentation from which multi-institutional validation can be built.

title: Single- Versus Two-Fraction HDR Brachytherapy Boost for Prostate Cancer: Long-Term Oncologic and Toxicity Outcomes.
abstract: Background and purpose High-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy boost with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) is an established dose-escalation strategy for high-risk prostate cancer, but the optimal number of HDR fractions is unclear. We compared oncological outcomes and toxicity between single- and two-fraction HDR boost. Materials and methods Retrospective cohort of 378 patients with localized prostate cancer treated as high risk by institutional criteria (D'Amico-based; regrouped by NCCN) in 2004-2016 with EBRT (46 Gy) and a CT-guided HDR boost. Before November 2009, patients received EBRT followed by two HDR fractions of 9-10 Gy 8 hours apart (n=205); from November 2009, a single 15 Gy fraction preceded EBRT (n=173). Biochemical recurrence-free (BRFS), metastasis-free, cancer-specific (CSFS), and grade ≥3 genitourinary (GUTFS) and gastrointestinal toxicity-free survival were estimated with Kaplan-Meier and compared with the log-rank test; Cox models were fitted. Results Median follow-up was 130.1 months (IQR 94-158). Single-fraction patients more often had cT3 disease (72.3% vs. 43.4%) and NCCN high or very high risk (84.4% vs. 67.8%). At 10 years, BRFS, MFS, and CSFS were 81.4%, 91.5%, and 95.4%, without significant differences between one and two fractions (BRFS 79.6% vs. 82.6%, p=0.784; CSFS 95.3% vs. 95.4%, p=0.992). Crude grade ≥3 GU toxicity was higher with two fractions (22.9% vs. 10.4%, p=0.002); 10-year GUTFS was 82.2% vs. 89.7% (p=0.076). PSA and Gleason score >7 independently predicted CSFS and BRFS. Conclusion In this non-randomized comparison of consecutive protocols, one and two HDR boost fractions showed no significant difference in long-term oncological control. The confidence intervals were wide, and equivalence was not tested. Two fractions had more grade ≥3 GU toxicity, which cannot be separated from treatment era, EBRT sequence, and follow-up. A single 15 Gy fraction appears adequate as a boost combined with EBRT. It does not apply to HDR monotherapy. Prospective confirmation is needed.

title: Feasibility of DLAS-Driven Reoptimization to Accelerate MR-guided Online Adaptive Radiotherapy for Abdominal Malignancies.
abstract: Purpose MR-guided online adaptive radiation therapy (MRgOART) adjusts for daily anatomical changes. One challenge is prolonged treatment time due to organs-at-risk (OARs) contour editing. Recently, deep learning auto-segmentation (DLAS) models have demonstrated accuracy on MRI images, reducing contour editing demands. In this retrospective study, we investigate the dosimetric impact of DLAS-driven MRgOART, in which daily adaptive plans are created directly using unedited DLAS contours, and the feasibility of a one-step contour and adaptive plan review and approval process. Methods Six patients treated for abdominal malignancies on a 1.5T MR-Linac were studied. Daily OAR anatomy was segmented by a MR-based DLAS model, with targets rigidly transferred from reference images. The DLAS-driven plan was generated by re-optimizing using unedited DLAS contours. Dose was recalculated using clinical contours for dosimetric comparison with the clinical plan. Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), mean distance-to-agreement (MDA), surface Dice Similarity Coefficient (sDSC), and relative added path length (rAPL) were used to compare geometric accuracy of DLAS to clinical contours. Target coverage, D0.03cc to the gastrointestinal OARs, and V1200cGy to kidneys and liver were used to assess plan quality. Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed-rank tests evaluated dosimetric differences between DLAS-driven and clinically delivered plans. Time savings for contour editing to plan approval were estimated. Results DLAS and clinical contours demonstrated good agreement, with most average DSC scores exceeding 0.8 and average MDA under 3mm for OARs. No significant differences were found in target coverage, D0.03cc, or V1200cGy between the clinically delivered and DLAS-driven plans. Estimated treatment time savings ranged from 8 to 24 minutes. Conclusions Accurate MR-based DLAS models may enable DLAS-driven adaptive planning, eliminating contour edits prior to reoptimization. DLAS-driven plans were comparable to clinically delivered plans for the six patients studied. DLAS-driven adaptive planning is a promising approach to reduce physician burden and treatment times in MRgOART.

title: Multimodal imaging evaluation of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery: A case report.
abstract: Giant coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) is a rare cardiovascular disease characterized by abnormal coronary dilatation and a high mortality rate. It lacks specific clinical manifestations and is often detected incidentally during imaging examinations, so early identification and timely intervention are crucial for improving patient prognosis. Existing studies have rarely documented the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, and clinical diagnostic and therapeutic experience remains to be further enriched. Here, we report a case of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery (LCX), incidentally detected by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) performed for palpitations. TTE and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast-enhanced echocardiography, and CT angiography (CTA) were combined to accurately evaluate the location, size, and adjacent anatomical relationship of the aneurysm, and a surgical plan was formulated accordingly. The patient recovered well after surgery. This case summarizes the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, offering a clinical reference for similar rare cases.

title: Diagnostic value of coronal CT imaging in a patient with cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia: A case report.
abstract: A 43-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and vomiting. Contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) with coronal reconstruction revealed marked dilatation of the ileocecal region, a whirl sign, a bird beak sign, and decreased enhancement of the ascending colon wall. The patient was diagnosed with cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia. Consequently, emergency surgery was performed. Intraoperative findings revealed 360° torsion of the ileum and ascending colon, with partial necrosis of the ascending colon wall. After resection of the twisted segment, functional end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The postoperative course was uneventful and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 11. Coronal CT imaging enabled the early diagnosis of cecal volvulus accompanied by intestinal ischemia and allowed prompt surgical intervention that resulted in a favorable outcome.

title: Interventional radiology management of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma.
abstract: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a rare, highly vascular tumor that occurs almost exclusively in adolescent and young adult males and is associated with substantial intraoperative bleeding risk during surgical resection. Preoperative intra-arterial embolization is commonly performed to reduce tumor vascularity and improve perioperative safety. We present a case of a 21-year-old male with a history of asthma presenting with persistent unilateral nasal congestion who was found to have a left-sided nasopharyngeal mass. Surgical pathology later confirmed sinonasal angiofibroma. Diagnostic cerebral angiography demonstrated tumor blush supplied by branches of the left sphenopalatine artery arising from the internal maxillary artery of the external carotid circulation without significant contribution from the internal carotid artery or ophthalmic artery anastomoses. Using a microcatheter system, selective catheterization of the left sphenopalatine artery was performed, and embolization was achieved with 200-micrometer polyethylene glycol microspheres until near stasis was observed. Postembolization angiography demonstrated marked reduction of tumor blush, consistent with successful devascularization. The patient subsequently underwent successful surgical resection with remarkably low intraoperative blood loss (estimated 50 mL). This case highlights the role of interventional radiology in targeted preoperative embolization for the management of juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. Selective embolization of the sphenopalatine arterial supply can significantly reduce tumor vascularity and facilitate safer surgical resection with minimal blood loss. The relatively insidious clinical presentation and use of polyethylene glycol microspheres, which, to our knowledge, have not been previously described in juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma, represent distinctive clinical and technical features of this case.

title: Isolated abdominal wall metastasis of endometrial carcinosarcoma: A case report.
abstract: Uterine carcinosarcoma, formerly called malignant mixed Müllerian tumor, is a rare and aggressive biphasic neoplasm made up of malignant epithelial and mesenchymal elements. Recurrence is frequent even after multimodal treatment, and distant relapses usually involve the lung, liver, or peritoneum. Isolated recurrence in the abdominal wall or subcutaneous tissue is rare and can easily be mistaken for a benign or unrelated soft-tissue lesion. A 71-year-old woman with hypertension and gout was diagnosed with grade 2 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma, staged IA on preoperative MRI. Surgical staging (total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy) revealed a carcinosarcoma with a predominantly endometrioid carcinomatous component, deep (>50%) myometrial invasion, endocervical stromal involvement, and lymphovascular invasion (pT2 N0). She received adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy with vaginal brachytherapy, followed by 6 cycles of paclitaxel-carboplatin, and remained disease-free for more than 3 years. Routine surveillance imaging then showed a new calcified mass in the anterior abdominal wall with an adjacent para-umbilical nodule. Percutaneous biopsy confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma whose immunohistochemical profile was consistent with the known gynecologic primary. With no disease elsewhere, she underwent wide local excision with mesh reconstruction, achieving clear margins, followed by radiotherapy to the surgical bed. Uterine carcinosarcoma can recur in unusual extra-pelvic soft-tissue sites years after seemingly successful treatment. Any new abdominal wall or subcutaneous lesion in these patients should be biopsied promptly and discussed in a multidisciplinary setting, as isolated recurrences may still be treated with curative intent.

title: Patient perceptions of artificial intelligence in MRI reconstruction: A mixed methods study from a single NHS trust.
abstract: Introduction As part of a strategy to increase magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) capacity, the UK government funded the purchase of manufacturer artificial intelligence (AI) MRI image reconstruction software on MRI scanners. It aimed to reduce scan duration without compromising image quality and has been widely installed on clinical MRI scanners across the UK. Methods This is a mixed methods study, using an initial questionnaire to quantify opinions followed by focus groups of responders to further explore their views on technical issues. Patient views on the use of AI in MRI image reconstruction for reducing acquisition times, and more generally in their MRI pathway, were assessed. Results Study participants prefer improved image quality over faster acquisition times. If reducing acquisition times with AI, they feel it should only be used if extremely accurate images can be ascertained. They are uncomfortable with the use of manufacturer AI software for image reconstruction where accuracy is not stated and would like to be told about the use of AI in MRI. Conclusions Many participants felt that manufacturer AI software for MRI image reconstruction may be used only if a high accuracy is demonstrated, and if the training data is representative of the patient population, to not exacerbate health inequalities. This information is not currently given by manufacturers, which made the patient representatives concerned. Implication for practice

title: Evaluation of image-matching and prostate movement angle using anatomical characteristics obtained from planning computed tomography.
abstract: Introduction Setup errors and prostate movement may be associated with individual patient anatomy and internal physiological conditions. We evaluated image-matching and angle of prostate movement during prostate radiotherapy using anatomical characteristics. Methods We included 103 patients who underwent prostate volumetric-modulated arc therapy. Body mass index (BMI) and the volumes of the lesser pelvic cavity, bladder, rectum, and prostate were measured using planning computed tomography. Patients were divided into small- and large-value groups according to the median value of each anatomical characteristic. The medians and standard deviations of bone setup errors and inter- and intra-fraction prostate movements were calculated in the anterior-posterior (AP), left-right (LR), and superior-inferior (SI) directions using pelvic bone and fiducial markers with the ExacTrac X-ray system. Prostate movement angles were calculated from the approximation equation of correlation between the AP and SI direction for both groups (rectum volume, bladder capacity). Results The average setup errors in the LR direction exhibited a moderate positively correlation (r = 0.43) with lesser pelvic cavity volume in the small-value group, and a moderate negative correlation (r = -0.45) in the large-value group, as determined by BMI and lesser pelvic cavity volume. Intra-fraction prostate movement angles were tilted 6.7° in the AP direction in the large rectal volume group and 3.1° in the SI direction in the large bladder volume group. Conclusions Image-matching and prostate movement angles differed between groups stratified according to patient anatomical characteristics, suggesting the potential utility of anisotropic margins and careful patient setup. Implications for practice Evaluating patient-specific anatomical characteristics before radiotherapy planning may help estimate susceptibility to setup errors and facilitate the definition of anisotropic margins based on individual prostate movement angle information.

title: Evaluation of the experience of imposter phenomenon in advanced practice and consultant therapeutic radiographers.
abstract: Introduction Research suggests a high prevalence of imposter phenomenon among healthcare professionals, which is associated with negative impacts on professional identity, performance, well-being, careers, and service development. This local NHS service evaluation explored the imposter phenomenon among advanced and consultant therapeutic radiographers in a single radiotherapy department. This research aimed to understand determinants and the impact of imposter phenomenon, and to investigate management strategies, generating recommendations for future practice. Methods This qualitative research adopted an interpretivist approach, utilising purposive homogeneous sampling in recruitment. Data collection was via semi-structured focus groups; data analysis was inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Researcher reflexivity and independent observer review enhanced the credibility and trustworthiness of findings. Results Four key themes were identified from the data. Imposter phenomenon was context-dependent, influenced by a complex blend of individual, interpersonal, and systemic factors. Most participants identified with feelings of imposter phenomenon and experienced surges throughout their careers. Organisational factors such as strong hierarchy, isolation, and lack of role clarity compounded imposter phenomenon. Peer comparison and perceived judgment were strong individual determinants. Management strategies included role planning, mentorship, peer support, clear development pathways, and reflective practice. Conclusion Clear role definition and career pathways, alongside interprofessional education, could reduce feelings of imposter phenomenon among advanced practice and consultant therapeutic radiographers. Individualised transition plans, mentorship, peer support, shared workspaces, and structured feedback can enhance confidence, collaboration, and performance. Implications for practice Organisational and professional guidance on career development, funding, workforce strategies, and strategic planning would support role efficacy, staff wellbeing, and retention, ultimately improving service delivery and patient care.

title: Experiences of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings and their communication: A systematic review of expectant parent and ultrasound Practitioner perspectives.
abstract: Introduction Current evidence suggests that the identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings are associated with negative psychological outcomes for both patients and ultrasound practitioners. There remains a need to synthesise and better understand this evidence to assess the extent and nature of the problem. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences, views and preferences of ultrasound practitioners and expectant parents regarding the identification and communication of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings. Methods Systematic review and narrative synthesis of studies reporting qualitative and quantitative data. The databases MEDLINE, CINAHL and Web-of-Science were searched between January-2010 and May-2026. Results Twelve studies were included. Findings highlight a lack of formal communication training and limited emotional support for practitioners when identifying and communicating adverse prenatal findings, contributing to anxiety, burnout, and role-related uncertainty. For patients, inadequate explanations, inconsistent communication, and insufficient time to process information were associated with immediate shock and longer-term psychological burden. Additionally, environmental and organisational factors, such as time pressures, workload, and suboptimal clinical settings, further influenced communication quality and exacerbated distress for both patients and practitioners. Conclusion Identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings have significant psychological impacts on patients and practitioners, influenced by communication quality. Ongoing gaps in training, emotional support, and role clarity contribute to inconsistent practice and increased distress, highlighting the need for structured frameworks and strengthened organisational support. Future research should evaluate communication interventions and include more diverse populations to improve psychological outcomes and consistency of care. Implications for practice Structured, empathetic communication of adverse findings should be supported by targeted training, clear role delineation, and organisational support to reduce psychological burden and improve consistency of care.
